body:
# 2026 Case OS Framework

## What it is
Methodology deck dated 2026-01-14 (created 2025-11-12). The named IP that underpins every Huify legal-vertical pitch: **Case Velocity = (Signed Cases × Avg Settlement × Settlement Rate) ÷ Settlement Cycle Time**. Frames why most firms overspend on marketing (tracking leads not outcomes, silos, no ad-spend-to-revenue link, gut feel not data), names the Legacy CRM Trap (Law Ruler as the canonical example), tells the Hansen & Rosasco transformation story with Shannon Quinn as the customer-voice anchor, and closes with a 1-Week Audit / 1-Month Diagnostic next-step menu.

## Strategic thesis
**Case Velocity is the operating metric that lets a plaintiff firm forecast revenue 3-6 months out instead of looking backward at what already happened.** Most firms can tell you what happened ("we signed 50 cases last month"). Top firms can predict what is coming ("50 cases × $75K × 60% settlement rate = $2.25M expected in 18 months = $125K/month velocity"). The framework's job is to convert plaintiff firms from backward-looking to forward-looking by tracking the data points Law Ruler never tracked (close dates, funding dates, source attribution).

The deeper move: **the Legacy CRM Trap frame.** Law Ruler is named explicitly. No source-to-settlement tracking. Rigid workflows requiring support to change. Only historical reporting, no forecasting. Data silos between teams. "Built for a different era. Became an operational bottleneck. You needed visibility. You got blind spots." This frame is reusable for any firm running on an old vertical-specific CRM that does not connect marketing to outcomes.

Third move: **Shannon Quinn as the customer-voice anchor**. "Shannon was working with this firm long before we got there. She saw the problem first. She championed the solution." Verbatim quote: "We were spending thousands on ads with no idea which ones led to settlements. Marketing and intake lived in different worlds. I knew we needed to close the loop." The framework's credibility hinges on Shannon's voice, not Huify's claim.

## What is interesting about this doc
The Case Velocity formula is the most reusable single artifact in the Huify legal corpus. Four variables, one ratio: Signed Cases (number of retainer agreements signed), Avg Settlement (average settlement value per case), Settlement Rate (% of cases that result in settlement), Cycle Time (average days from signed to funded). All four are measurable in HubSpot once you migrate off Law Ruler. The formula converts marketing spend conversations from abstract ROI debates into specific lever pulls.

The "What Hansen & Rosasco Can Do Now" outcomes list (track every marketing dollar to actual case value, forecast revenue 3-6 months out, identify and fix bottlenecks real-time, make budget decisions on data not gut, provide transparent referral partner experience) is the visible proof of the framework. Each line is a capability that did not exist before the Case OS build.

The "Why This Makes H&R the Go-To 9/11 Referral Partner" close converts the operational outcome into a business outcome: "transparent intake process builds trust, real-time visibility into case status, proven systems for tracking and accountability, no case falls through the cracks." This is the pitch to referring attorneys, not just the firm itself. The framework produces a marketing position, not just a reporting capability.

The "Old Way vs Case Velocity" comparison slide is the moment that lands the framework. "We signed 50 cases last month" + "but when will they pay out, which sources convert faster, where are bottlenecks?" + shrug = the old way. The right side: "50 cases × $75K × 60% = $2.25M expected in 18 months = $125K/month velocity, track if you're on pace, fix slowdowns NOW." This is the slide that converts a passive observer into a buyer.

The discussion prompts throughout ("When a new case comes in at 8pm on a Friday, how does it get to the right person?" / "If I asked your intake coordinator and case manager where a case is, would they give the same answer?" / "Should we spend more on radio or Facebook? What data do you pull?" / "What's the one bottleneck in your case operations that would have the biggest impact if you fixed it?") are designed to surface gaps in real-time during the deck walkthrough. The framework deck is also a discovery instrument.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any plaintiff firm pitch, legal-vertical methodology, or marketing-spend-to-revenue narrative:

1. **Case Velocity formula** (Signed Cases × Avg Settlement × Settlement Rate ÷ Settlement Cycle Time). Drop into any plaintiff firm conversation about marketing ROI.
2. **The Legacy CRM Trap frame** (no source-to-settlement, rigid workflows, only historical reporting, data silos). Drop into any firm currently on Law Ruler, Litify, Filevine, or legacy practice management.
3. **Looking Backward vs Looking Forward comparison slide** (cases signed last month vs predicted revenue + when + cycle metrics). Drop into any pitch where buyer has retrospective metrics but no forward-looking ones.
4. **Shannon Quinn customer-voice quote** ("We were spending thousands on ads with no idea which ones led to settlements"). Drop into any legal-vertical pitch with permission.
5. **"What Shannon Saw First" credibility frame** (customer championed the solution before vendor arrived). Drop into any pitch where the buyer's own champion was already pushing the change.
6. **Discussion prompts at section breaks** (Friday 8pm new case + intake/case manager status agreement + radio vs Facebook spend + biggest bottleneck). Drop into any framework deck to convert pitch into discovery.
7. **"In 6 months / In 12 months" predictive promise** ("In 6 months you'll have predictive velocity data, in 12 months you'll forecast revenue with confidence"). Drop into any framework that requires time-series data to mature.
8. **"What Hansen & Rosasco Can Do Now" outcome list** (5 capabilities that didn't exist before). Drop into any case study or transformation deck.
9. **"Why This Makes H&R the Go-To Referral Partner" business outcome frame** (operational capability -> referring-attorney market position). Drop into any pitch where the operational outcome enables a new business outcome.
10. **1-Week Audit / 1-Month Diagnostic two-step next-step menu**. Drop into any low-commitment-to-medium-commitment progression.

## ROI / outcome / story
**The formula in plain numbers:**
- 50 cases × $75K × 60% = $2.25M expected
- Over 18 months = $125K/month velocity
- Now trackable and forecastable in HubSpot

**What you're tracking now (vs Law Ruler):**
- Date case signed
- Date case moved to litigation
- Date settlement reached
- Date funding received
- Source attribution from first touch
- Every stage transition with timestamps

- Track leads, not outcomes

- No ad-spend-to-revenue link

**The Legacy CRM Trap (Law Ruler specifically):**
- No source-to-settlement tracking
- Rigid workflows require support to change

**Reusable Shannon quote for any legal pitch:**
"We were spending thousands on ads with no idea which ones led to settlements. Marketing and intake lived in different worlds. I knew we needed to close the loop." - Shannon Quinn, Marketing Manager, Hansen & Rosasco

Shannon Quinn championed the source-to-settlement framing internally before Huify formalized it. **This doc** (2025-11-12 created, 2026-01-14 modified): Case OS Framework deck formalized as named methodology. **Active use**: as of 2026-05 named in [[carpenter-chartered-cosell-playbook]] as the Josh-led segment of the joint call. **Next**: framework deck likely evolves with each new legal proof point (Carpenter, Petroff Amshen, SEDA). **Long arc**: Case Velocity becomes the durable Huify intellectual property anchor for legal vertical, the same way "audit-to-retainer" is the IP anchor for the broader services motion in [[tortscale-readinessaudit-gtm-operating-plan-v2]].

body:
# Forge Brain Extraction Methodology

## What it is
The repeatable protocol for scanning Drive content, classifying it, and enriching it into summary cards for the josh-identity / forge-dashboard system. Designed so future sessions (this agent or another) can pick up where the prior session left off without losing pattern consistency. The methodology produces a node-per-file but clusters nodes around clients and types of work.

## Why this exists
Three failure modes this prevents:
1. **Pattern drift**: a future session writes summaries that look different from the existing 28 cards. The cockpit graph stops being legible.
2. **Re-ingest waste**: a future session re-summarizes a file that already has a card. Wasted tokens.
3. **Missing the why**: a future session writes factual summaries that don't surface strategy, reuse, ROI, or evolution. The brain becomes a card catalog instead of an operating asset.

## The pipeline (in order)

### Step 1: Enumerate
- Query Drive folder by parentId to list all files + subfolders
- For client archives: start from the Clients folder (0B5FSdnb1o2ycLUkwaE5Fd1BJcHM) or Archives (0B9xKKkhWsRi-LWE4OEJjUklSY28)
- Exclude obvious junk: duplicate PDF/Doc pairs, shortcuts, system files
- Capture: id, title, mimeType, createdTime, modifiedTime, parentId, owner

### Step 2: Classify
- **Entity boundary**: josh | huify | shared. Default to huify for client work. Personal-only goes to josh.
- **Type** (matches josh-identity schema): deal, client, playbook, doc, project, idea, rule, skill, scheduled-skill
- **Lead vs Client**: anything in "Leads - Lower Funnel" or active-deal-stage is type=deal. Anything in "Clients" folder or archived clients is type=client. Methodology docs are type=playbook.
- **Era assignment**: by createdTime, map to one of the 8 eras in [[huify-firm-evolution-timeline]]
- **Cluster assignment**: which client folder is this file inside? That becomes the cluster parent.

### Step 3: Drill
- For folder-level summaries: enumerate contents but do not necessarily read every file
- For high-value files: read content via `read_file_content` MCP call
- For files exceeding read limit: note path, skip body, summarize from title + metadata
- For PDFs that match a Doc: process only the Doc (skip the PDF)
- For obvious duplicates (same title with version suffix): process the latest only

### Step 4: Summarize (the card)
Each card has 9 sections plus frontmatter:

1. **What it is** (1-2 factual sentences)
2. **Strategic thesis** (the bet, the play, the worldview embedded)
3. **What is interesting about this** (non-obvious moves, surprise findings, the thing to remember 6 months out)
4. **Reusable assets** (numbered list of named patterns with "drop into X" guidance)
5. **ROI / outcome / story** (dollar figures, hero quotes, transformation arcs; for pre-outcome: what success looks like)
6. **How this relates** (typed relationships: proof source, sibling pattern, deal feeder, era position)
7. **Evolution** (earlier / this doc / next / long arc)
8. **When to consult this in the future** (retrieval hooks: "if you're prepping for X, this is the precedent")
9. **Cross-links** (heavy wikilinks; pattern-level nodes get their own wikilink even if they don't have a card yet)

Plus open enrichment items at the bottom for things future sessions can deepen.

### Step 5: Frontmatter contract
Required fields (match josh-identity contract):
- `id`: kebab-case slug, stable, unique
- `name`: human-readable label
- `type`: one of the schema types
- `scope`: more specific shape within type (strategy-brief, deal-prep, era-cluster, etc.)
- `department`: sales, clients, marketing, revops, strategy, personal
- `priority`: high, medium, low
- `status`: active, archived, signed, pre-decision, etc.
- `last_activity`: ISO date
- `tags`: free-form array

Extension fields (source provenance):
- `source_type`: drive, gmail, slack, gong, web, calendar, synthesis
- `source_id`: native ID (Drive file ID, etc.)
- `source_url`: link back to original
- `source_mime`: mime type if applicable
- `captured_at`: when ingest happened (ISO)
- `original_created_at`: when source was created (ISO)
- `entity`: josh | huify | shared
- `people`: array of names
- `companies`: array of company names
- `frameworks_invoked`: array of named patterns this doc uses
- `proof_referenced`: array of other cards/stories cited as proof
- `proof_strength`: hero | secondary | candidate | pre-decision | stub | preserved-reference
- `importance`: high | medium | low
- `deal_value`: dollar amount or range if applicable

### Step 6: Cross-link discipline
Wikilinks are the load-bearing edges of the graph:
- Every card links backward to predecessors (earlier client, earlier methodology, previous version)
- Every card links forward to successors (next deal, next era, next pattern application)
- Every card links sideways to siblings (other clients in same era, parallel methodologies)
- Pattern-level wikilinks get their own nodes: `[[wedge-dont-dilute-pattern]]`, `[[advisor-frame-pattern]]`, `[[case-velocity-formula]]`
- Pattern nodes don't need their own cards yet — they emerge from the graph as hubs
- Format: `[[id-slug]]` where id-slug matches another card's `id:` field

### Step 7: Save and report
- Write to `outputs/forge-extraction/clients/<id>.md` for client/era/methodology cards
- Write to `outputs/forge-extraction/drive/<id>.md` for individual Drive file cards
- Update extraction state log (which IDs are done, which are queued)
- After every 3-5 cards: send a SendUserMessage status update

## How to prioritize what to drill next
Rank by:
1. **Strategic importance to current motion**: any file referenced by an active 2026 deal or methodology card jumps to top
2. **Methodology origin**: any client folder that contains the first instance of a named pattern (e.g., Bronson/Napoli for Rosetta Stone)
3. **Era anchor**: the 1-2 most-load-bearing clients per era
4. **Outcome richness**: clients with documented dollar outcomes (H&R, Carpenter $150K, Mediafly $75K)
5. **Breadth signal**: clients whose folders contain 20+ files indicate multi-month engagements worth detailed enumeration

Deprioritize:
- One-file engagements that don't connect to anything
- Internal admin/accounting files unless they reveal financial structure
- Duplicate versions (PDF + Doc of same content)
- Stub files (titles only, no body content)

## What to mark for human verification
Flag in each card's "Open enrichment items" section:
- Dollar amounts that need confirmation
- Methodology origin claims that need confirmation
- Names that need ID verification
- Whether a doc is still active vs archived

## State tracking
- `outputs/forge-extraction/state/drive_manifest.json` has the current ingest queue
- Update with each completed card
- Future sessions read this first to know what's done

## Quality gates (when is a card "done")
A card is done when:
1. All 9 sections are filled (no placeholder TODO text)
2. Frontmatter has all required fields plus relevant extension fields
3. At least 3 cross-links to existing cards
4. At least 1 named methodology pattern in `frameworks_invoked`
5. The "When to consult this" section has at least 4 specific retrieval hooks
6. ROI/outcome section has either real numbers or explicit "pre-outcome" framing
7. Open enrichment items section names what future drilling can add

A card is NOT done if:
- It only summarizes facts without strategic thesis
- It has no cross-links (orphaned node)
- It uses generic language ("this is a great document")
- It hides uncertainty behind authoritative claims

## File-level cards within client clusters
When a client cluster has 20+ files (Bronson/Napoli, Hansen & Rosasco, Petroff Amshen):
- First write the client overview card (the cluster hub)
- Then write individual file cards for the 5-10 highest-leverage files in the folder
- Each file card frontmatter includes `parent_client_cluster: <client-card-id>`
- File card body is shorter than client card (4-6 sections) but follows same shape
- Cross-link from file card back to parent client card and forward to where this file's pattern is reused

## Common patterns recognized so far
This methodology has produced these named pattern nodes that recur across cards. Each is a candidate for its own pattern card someday:
- advisor-frame-pattern
- audit-to-retainer-pattern
- black-box-problem-frame
- case-velocity-formula
- closing-culture-brand
- day-14-out-clause-pattern
- decision-framework-with-our-read
- eight-partnership-principles
- four-paths-with-no-sale-option
- hard-kill-checkpoint-pattern
- hubspot-onboarding-waiver-timing
- keep-what-works-pitch
- kill-switch-30-days-pattern
- lane-split-rules
- milestone-gated-expansion-pattern
- minute-by-minute-agenda-pattern
- named-bets-pattern
- pairing-method-pattern
- partner-doc-vs-team-doc-split
- phase-1-parallel-build-pattern
- plus-one-subscription-pattern
- quick-start-sprint-pattern
- rosetta-stone-terminology-mapping
- smallest-viable-experiment-pattern
- three-lane-offer-pattern
- three-option-pricing-pattern
- transparency-about-bias-pattern
- two-engine-model-pattern
- v1-to-v2-pivot-pattern
- warm-only-outbound-pattern
- we-heard-you-rescope-pattern
- wedge-dont-dilute-pattern
- what-i-heard-opener-pattern
- working-document-not-proposal-frame

These will emerge as graph hubs in the cockpit even without their own cards.

## How to use this methodology
At the start of any future scanning session:
1. Read this file
2. Read the latest manifest in `state/`
3. Pick the next priority item per the ranking rules above
4. Execute Steps 1-7 of the pipeline
5. Send status update after every 3-5 cards
6. At session end, update state and write a brief session log

# Blue Fox Trading - Decision Summary (Sprint chosen)

## What it is
Closing artifact dated 2026-04-23, sent same day as the 1pm Blueprint walkthrough ([[blue-fox-trading-implementation-blueprint]]). Confirms Zach chose Sprint: 2 weeks, $7,000 fixed fee, Phase 1 migration and setup only. Provides activation link for one-click e-signature, the deliverables list, the timeline, the open questions parked for Monday's review with Caleb, the long-term partnership roadmap (Walk -> Expansion -> Partnership Plan), and Zach's named fears mapped to how Sprint protects against each.

## Strategic thesis
**Confirm what was decided in the room, not what you wished was decided.** The doc explicitly names Zach's reasoning in his own words: "you are running Blue Fox alongside Hire Harper, HealthHire, and Marriott consulting work; you are 19 days into the freight brokerage; Caleb is minimally involved on the freight side; and you want to prove the migration before committing to the bigger build. Sprint matches that reality exactly." Confirming the buyer's reasoning back to them is the move that holds the decision once the room is empty.

The deeper move: **the explicit "what you are NOT being asked to commit to" section.** Four items: Phase 2 Walk (no commitment until Sprint exit review), Marketing Hub or Commerce Hub (parked to Phase 3), any 12-month retainer or lock-in (30-day kill switch applies), scope changes if 48-hour data audit reveals bigger problems (written adjustment before any work changes). This neutralizes commitment-fatigue at the moment of signature.

Third move: **the activation link as one-click e-signature.** "Click, review, e-sign." Single URL. Mobile-friendly. "Ideally signed Thursday afternoon to preserve the HubSpot onboarding waiver." Compresses the procurement cycle from days to minutes.

## What is interesting about this doc
The HubSpot onboarding waiver section is the operational rigor. "$1,500 normally charged for onboarding. Waived when you engage Huify as your implementation partner. The waiver applies cleanly when both sides sign around the same time." The doc explicitly flags the timing risk: "If there is a long gap between your Sales Hub Pro signing tomorrow and the Huify quote signing, HubSpot may process the onboarding fee before the waiver takes effect." Naming the timing dependency converts a procedural footnote into a deal-acceleration lever.

The "Where this goes next, after Sprint" section is the disciplined upsell deferral. Phase 2 Walk (automation engine after Sprint sign-off). Phase 3 Expansion (Commerce Hub for invoicing, Marketing Hub for SDVOSB carrier network - "10,000 veteran-owned carriers is an ICP no one else has"). Partnership Plan (12-month engagement with revenue-aligned pricing, Month 2+ option). Each future phase is named but not sold today. "Not part of Sprint, but worth discussing once you see Sprint results."

The fears-table is reduced to 5 rows here (vs 7 in the blueprint) and rephrased as direct buyer-vs-seller. "$22,000 a month on Bullhorn with no usage" → "Sprint is $7,000 total, two weeks, fixed fee. 99% cheaper than your Bullhorn year 1." The "99% cheaper" framing is the most reusable line in the corpus.

The "What we are asking from you" section is sequenced by urgency: (1) sign the Huify quote at activation link, ideally Thursday afternoon, no later than Monday to keep May 1 kickoff; (2) bring Caleb (and if available Ariana) to Monday's 11:30am ET call so we close the remaining gates in one conversation; (3) by Monday, answer the 5 open questions (Ascend, DAT, email system, finance approver, Ariana's role).

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any post-walkthrough close, sprint commit, or one-click-sign motion:

1. **Activation link pattern** (one-click e-signature, single URL, mobile-friendly). Drop into any time-bounded close.
2. **"What you decided" with buyer reasoning in their own words**. Drop into any post-meeting close email.
3. **"What you are NOT being asked to commit to" section** (4 items: phase 2 scope, parked phases, retainer/lock-in, scope changes from audit). Drop into any sign-now-but-don't-overcommit close.
4. **"Where this goes next, after Sprint" disciplined roadmap** (Phase 2 Walk -> Phase 3 Expansion -> Partnership Plan, each named not sold). Drop into any phased engagement close.
5. **HubSpot onboarding waiver timing flag** (sign both sides same day or close to it). Drop into any HubSpot Solutions Partner cosell close.
6. **"99% cheaper than your Bullhorn year 1" math comparison** (compares to buyer's named prior-vendor pain). Drop into any pitch where buyer has stated prior-vendor spend.
7. **Three-things-asked-in-order-of-urgency** (sign / bring stakeholders / answer open questions). Drop into any pre-kickoff close.
8. **Five open questions parked for Monday** (specific items, named). Drop into any pre-kickoff to ensure clarity.
9. **"Text me with questions before you sign"** with mobile number. Drop into any close to keep the channel open.
10. **"Anything we adjust, we adjust in writing before signature, not after"**. Drop into any close to prevent post-signature scope arguments.

## ROI / outcome / story
**The deal:**
- Sprint chosen: 2 weeks, $7,000 fixed fee, Phase 1 only
- HubSpot Sales Hub Pro license separate (billed by HubSpot)
- HubSpot onboarding fee waived (~$1,500 savings via Huify partnership)

**Sprint deliverables:**
- HubSpot portal audit with written findings
- Carrier custom object finalized (V2 refinement of card Zach already built)
- Up to 10,000 carriers imported from spreadsheet to HubSpot-usable state
- Carriers tagged by lane and equipment type (reefer, flatbed, Conestoga, sea, air, intermodal)

# Blue Fox Trading - Implementation Blueprint

## What it is
Working document for Zach Hyre / Blue Fox Trading Co dated 2026-04-22, walked through live in a 1pm ET session. Frames three forward paths (Option A Sprint $6K-$8K, Option B Full Crawl $12K-$15K, Option C Committed Plan $40K-$50K bundled 12-week) for a 19-day-old freight brokerage spin-up. Captures everything heard across three prior calls, names the cost of waiting ($210K/week to competitors), addresses Zach's named fears (Bullhorn trauma, dead-stock tools, $100K systems nobody uses), commits to eight partnership principles, walks through a 5-question decision framework with pre-filled "our read" answers, and explicitly says "this is a working document, not a proposal."

## Strategic thesis
**Direction, not dollars. Working document, not proposal.** The doc explicitly frames what is being decided today (direction, fit, which questions still need answers) vs what is NOT being decided (exact price, final scope, who signs, which broker pilots, Caleb's involvement, any specific answer still needed). This converts a sales call from a yes/no transaction into a shared-design exercise. "Nothing is locked until Thursday's joint call. Everything today is still clay."

The deeper move: **eight partnership principles applied to every engagement we run.** Look at data before committing (48h audit, written report before signature). Agree on "done" before starting (testable checkpoints). Pilot before scale (one broker first). No wasted meetings (written agenda, time cap, decision output). Track adoption weekly (logins, deals touched, workflow completions). You text me, not a ticket queue (24h escalation, cell phone). Team you meet is team you keep (no handoff to customer success). Kill switch keeps us honest (30 days written notice, no clawback). Each principle is built specifically against one of Zach's named fears.

Third move: **decision framework with pre-filled "our read" answers**. Five questions (urgency of same-day load channel, when 10 new brokers start, carrier data confidence, Caleb's time commitment, your gut). For three of them, Josh names Huify's read with reasoning. The buyer can correct in real-time. "Scan your answers. If three or more cluster on the same path, that is usually the right path." This is co-decision design, not sales pressure.

## What is interesting about this doc
The orange-callout / blue-callout system is the operational rigor. Orange = "commitments Huify makes to you." Blue = "questions we answer together during this session." The buyer sees the working state visually, not just in prose. This is the most reusable formatting pattern in the entire Huify deal corpus.

The "What we heard" section is unusually patient. Three sub-sections (the business, the vision, your fears) each end with a "Discussing together" prompt. Naming Zach's north star verbatim ("make the business work for itself") is the kind of customer-voice anchor that makes everything that follows feel grounded. The vision walkthrough (shipper emails -> HubSpot parses -> deal created -> top 5 carriers surfaced by lane/equipment/reliability -> quote requests -> winner picked -> brokers focus on relationships) is the buyer's own future-state described back to him.

The "$210K per week" opportunity cost frame is the math anchor. 50 loads/day × $300-$600 gross profit = $15K-$30K/day. Weekly = $105K-$210K. Annual = $5M-$7M+. Payback period across any of the three paths: 1-3 weeks. "Payback runs faster than onboarding. That math is what makes starting rational. Not starting is the risky move."

The fears table is unusually candid. Each row has Zach's verbatim concern paired with the specific design move that addresses it. "Bullhorn took two months and I hated it" → "Phase 1 capped at four weeks. Stand-ups capped at 30 minutes with written agendas. No vague meetings. No drawn-out discovery." Most sales decks list fears generically; this one mirrors named fears with named mitigations.

The "What we are trying to accomplish together" section (5 outcomes) is the explicit scope contract. "By the end of Phase 2 (twelve weeks from kickoff), we agree these five outcomes define success." Then the disarming follow-up: "These are paraphrased from your own words. The wording is ours. The ambition is yours."

The "Out of scope" section is unusually explicit. Phase 1 NOT in scope: Marketing Hub campaigns to new leads, Commerce Hub for ACH/credit checks, AI-driven outbound, cross-company integration with the recruitment business, mobile app, reporting beyond standard HubSpot, training for brokers not yet hired. Phase 2 NOT in scope: recruitment company migration, VA medical coding sister company, 7,500-business veteran network activation, Service Hub for customer support ticketing. "If you want anything from this list in scope, we document it, estimate it, and bring it into a future phase. We do not absorb it silently."

The "What we need before kickoff" section converts the decision into a procurement checklist: 4 technical gates (Ascend TMS version, DAT API access, email system, HubSpot admin access), 3 stakeholder confirmations (Caleb's email + Phase 1 exit review confirmation, finance approver, pilot broker), 3 business context items (sample shipper emails, sample carrier spreadsheet, list of preferred carriers).

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any working-document-not-proposal, multi-shape decision, or freight/logistics deal:

1. **"Working document, not a proposal" frame** with explicit "what we are deciding today" vs "what we are NOT deciding today" sections. Drop into any high-stakes pre-close meeting.
2. **Orange/Blue callout system** (orange = Huify commitments, blue = questions answered together). Drop into any working document or live-walkthrough deck.
3. **Eight partnership principles** (data before commit / agree on done / pilot before scale / no wasted meetings / weekly adoption / text me not ticket queue / same team / kill switch). Drop into any services engagement to define how you partner.
4. **Decision framework with pre-filled "our read"** (5 questions, Huify names its read with reasoning for 3 of them, buyer corrects in real-time). Drop into any complex sales decision.
5. **"What we heard" three-section structure** (the business / the vision / your fears) each ending with a "Discussing together" prompt. Drop into any discovery recap.
6. **Cost-of-waiting math at weekly granularity** ("every week the current setup persists, competitors are winning $210,000"). Drop into any pitch where the buyer can articulate their lost daily/weekly volume.
7. **Fears table with verbatim quote + named mitigation** (one row per fear, one design move per row). Drop into any pitch to a buyer with prior-vendor trauma.
8. **"What we are trying to accomplish together" 5-outcome contract** with explicit "paraphrased from your own words, wording is ours, ambition is yours." Drop into any scope-defining conversation.
9. **Three-shape options (Sprint / Full Crawl / Committed)** with explicit "best for you if" criteria per shape. Drop into any productized-services menu where buyer commitment level varies.
10. **Out-of-scope explicit listing** (Phase 1 NOT / Phase 2 NOT with "we do not absorb silently" language). Drop into any SOW to neutralize scope-creep.
11. **"What we need before kickoff" procurement checklist** (technical gates / stakeholder confirmations / business context items). Drop into any pre-kickoff document.
12. **HubSpot onboarding waiver timing logic** ($1,500 waived when Huify partnership signs around same time as HubSpot, applies to all three paths). Drop into any HubSpot Solutions Partner cosell.
13. **"Discussing together" prompts at section ends** (forces real-time conversation instead of one-way pitch). Drop into any walkthrough deck.
14. **"Our read" pre-filled answers with explicit "correct us if you see it differently"**. Drop into any decision framework to anchor without overreaching.

## ROI / outcome / story
**The math (Zach's own numbers via Miguel):**
- 50 loads/day at target volume
- $300-$600 gross profit per load
- Daily opportunity cost: $15K-$30K
- Weekly opportunity cost: $105K-$210K
- Annual opportunity cost: $5M-$7M+
- Payback period across any path: 1-3 weeks

**Three shapes at a glance:**
- Option A Sprint: 2 weeks, $6K-$8K. Data audit + 10K carriers imported + tagged + reliability tiers + Breeze AI demo + integration scoping. Best if data state unknown, or you want lowest cash risk.
- Option B Full Crawl: 4 weeks, $12K-$15K. Sprint + zach.ships email parsing + Breeze AI in production + carrier match workflow + quote request sequence + one broker running real loads. Best if you trust the model and want a broker live by Week 4.
- Option C Committed Plan: 12 weeks, $40K-$50K (bundled 10% savings). Full Crawl + Phase 2 (deal pipeline automations + broker KPI dashboard + DAT + Ascend TMS + 10-broker onboarding playbook). Best if you need all 15 brokers live by mid-July.

**Five outcomes by end of Phase 2 (Week 12):**
1. Revenue channel open: same-day loads captured, $15K+/day gross revenue
2. Team lives in HubSpot: 15 brokers at 80%+ weekly engagement, nobody in spreadsheets
3. Zach out of the middle: system surfaces top 5, sends quote requests, handles routine coordination
4. Network internal first: 2,500+ carriers in active rotation with reliability scores. DAT is backup, not primary.
5. Business grows without you: reports + tweaks + focus on next thing

**Adoption KPIs:**
- Loads/day Phase 1: 5+, Phase 2: 15+
- Same-day loads captured Phase 1: 2+, Phase 2: 10+
- Gross revenue/day Phase 1: ~$3K, Phase 2: $9K+
- Response time Phase 1: 30 min, Phase 2: 15 min
- Carriers in rotation Phase 1: 500+, Phase 2: 2,500+
- Weekly team activity Phase 1: 100% of 1 pilot, Phase 2: 80%+ of 15

**Outcome:** Zach chose Sprint ($7K, 2 weeks). See [[blue-fox-trading-decision-summary]] for the closing artifact.

## How this relates
- **Companion close**: [[blue-fox-trading-decision-summary]] (the email post-walkthrough confirming Sprint chosen at $7K)
- **Companion SOW**: [[blue-fox-trading-sprint-sow]] (the legal terms)
- **Earlier intro**: [[blue-fox-trading-intro-call-zach]] (the first conversation)
- **Channel partner**: Miguel at HubSpot is the AE managing Sales Hub Pro license; HubSpot onboarding waiver applies when both sides sign close to same day
- **Sibling Sprint sales motion**: same shape as [[tortscale-readinessaudit-gtm-operating-plan-v2]]'s $5K Sprint and [[seda-law-decision-summary]]'s Option C lean start. All converge on the under-CFO-discretionary-spend entry point.
- **Vertical**: freight brokerage / logistics - tertiary ICP (manufacturing-adjacent) per [[tortscale-readinessaudit-gtm-operating-plan-v2]]
- **GTM v2 deal**: Blue Fox does not appear in [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]]'s open pipeline (that doc was 2026-05-08; Blue Fox kickoff May 1). It is in flight outside that snapshot.
- **Bullhorn trauma reference**: $22K/mo, 2 months, hated it. The deal hinges on not repeating that pattern.

## Evolution
**Earlier**: 3 prior calls with Zach. Customs brokerage SDVOSB established. Freight brokerage spin-up Feb 2026 (19 days in at time of pitch). 10K carriers in spreadsheet stuck at 1,000-row free-tier cap. **This doc** (2026-04-22): 1pm ET blueprint walkthrough. **Same day**: Decision Summary sent ([[blue-fox-trading-decision-summary]]) - Sprint chosen at $7K. **2026-04-23 11am ET**: joint signing call with Miguel (Sales Hub Pro + Huify SOW). **2026-04-27 (Monday)**: Phase 1 kickoff. Actual kickoff slipped to 2026-05-01 per SOW. **2026-05-15**: Sprint exit review and sign-off. **Long arc**: Phase 2 Walk (automation engine), Phase 3 Expansion (Commerce Hub + Marketing Hub for SDVOSB carrier network), potential Partnership Plan (revenue-aligned pricing 12-month).

## When to consult this in the future

# Blue Fox Trading - Phase 1 Sprint SOW

## What it is
Formal Statement of Work between Huify LLC and Blue Fox Trading Co. dated 2026-04-23 for the $7,000 Phase 1 Sprint chosen in [[blue-fox-trading-decision-summary]]. 15 numbered sections covering parties, engagement, scope, timeline, fees, acceptance criteria, kill switch, client and Huify responsibilities, data caveat, what's out of Sprint scope (Phase 2 Walk), long-term partnership option, confidentiality, governing law (Virginia), acceptance. Executable via activation link.

## Strategic thesis
**Make the legal terms readable enough that the buyer signs same day.** The SOW is unusually conversational for a legal document. Each section is short, named, and direct. Section 7 (Kill Switch) is one paragraph: "Either party may terminate this SOW with 30 days written notice. If terminated before the Sprint exit review, Client pays for work performed through the termination date on a pro-rated basis against the $7,000 fixed fee. No claw-back of payments for work already delivered. Phase 2 Walk is not automatically implied; Client is under no obligation to continue." That's the entire termination clause. Most SOWs have 3 paragraphs of indemnification language doing the same thing.

The deeper move: **Section 10 Data Caveat as a pre-committed scope adjustment.** "If the 48-hour data audit reveals the data is materially worse than represented, Huify will deliver a written scope adjustment for Client's review before additional work is performed. No scope expansion happens silently." This converts the most-common services-delivery dispute (the data was worse than we thought, we want more money) into a pre-agreed workflow. The buyer cannot be surprised by a scope adjustment because the SOW says how scope adjustments happen.

Third move: **Section 12 Partnership Plan as a placeholder, not a sale.** "Huify offers a twelve-month Partnership Plan with revenue-aligned pricing for clients who want Huify deeply embedded in their operation. The Partnership Plan is not part of this Sprint SOW. If Client wishes to explore it after Sprint exit, Huify will scope and present terms for Month 2 or later consideration." Names the future product without selling it. Reserves the right to come back.

## What is interesting about this doc
The Section 4 Timeline table maps SOW execution -> kickoff -> data audit -> import -> Breeze demo -> Phase 2 scoping -> exit review across 14 days. Each milestone has a target date and a named owner. Most SOWs have a single "duration" line; this one has 7 named gates.

The Section 6 Acceptance Criteria are explicit and testable: 10,000 records imported with lane and equipment data present, Breeze AI returns useful matching results, data quality report delivered, Phase 2 scoping doc delivered, portal audit findings delivered, Client acknowledges receipt. "Useful matching results" is the only soft criterion; the rest are binary.

The Section 9 Huify Responsibilities point that says "Maintain the same team (Josh, Ben, Erika) across the engagement — no handoffs to customer success in the middle" is unusual legal language. Most agencies preserve the right to substitute team members. This commitment converts the partnership principle from a pitch line into a contractual obligation.

The "Huify begins new engagements on the 1st and 15th of each month" line in Section 4 is the operational rigor that prevents the agency from over-committing. Naming the cadence makes the next kickoff date predictable, even if the SOW slips.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any productized-services Sprint SOW:

1. **Conversational SOW format** (short numbered sections, direct language, no boilerplate). Drop into any productized engagement.
2. **Kill switch clause** (30 days written notice, pro-rated through termination date, no clawback, Phase 2 not automatically implied). Drop into any retainer or sprint SOW.
3. **Data Caveat section** (48h audit, written scope adjustment before additional work, no silent scope expansion). Drop into any SOW where data quality is a variable.
4. **Acceptance Criteria as testable bullets** (5-6 binary items + 1 soft). Drop into any deliverable-based SOW.
5. **Timeline table with named owner per milestone**. Drop into any time-bounded engagement.
6. **"Maintain the same team" responsibility line** (no handoff to customer success). Drop into any SOW where team continuity is part of the pitch.
7. **Kickoff on 1st or 15th of month rule**. Drop into any agency SOW to manage capacity.
8. **Section 11 Out-of-Scope explicit list** (what's NOT in Sprint, to be priced separately if added). Drop into any phased-services SOW.
9. **Section 12 Partnership Plan placeholder** (future product named, not sold in this SOW). Drop into any SOW to reserve future revenue without bloating current scope.
10. **Activation-link execution method** (signature via URL or signed below). Drop into any one-click-sign motion.

## ROI / outcome / story
**The SOW terms:**
- Fee: $7,000 USD fixed fee
- Payment: invoiced by Huify, payable within 15 days
- HubSpot license: separate (paid to HubSpot directly)
- HubSpot onboarding fee: waived via Huify partnership ($1,500 savings)
- Governing law: Virginia
- Dispute resolution: good-faith negotiation first, binding arbitration if it fails
- Confidentiality: survives termination for 2 years

**Timeline (per SOW Section 4):**
- 2026-04-25: SOW executed (activation link signed)
- 2026-05-01: Kickoff
- 2026-05-03: Data audit complete, written report delivered
- 2026-05-08: Carrier import and object finalization
- 2026-05-12: Breeze AI demo session
- 2026-05-14: Phase 2 Walk scoping doc delivered
- 2026-05-15: Sprint exit review (sign-off)

**Acceptance criteria (Section 6):**
1. 10,000 carrier records imported and live in HubSpot with lane and equipment data present
2. Breeze AI returns useful matching results on representative queries
3. Written data quality report delivered
4. Written Phase 2 Walk scoping document delivered
5. Portal audit written findings delivered
6. Client acknowledges receipt of all deliverables in Section 3

**Client responsibilities (Section 8):**
- Admin HubSpot portal access within 48h of kickoff
- Sample 10K-carrier spreadsheet within 48h of kickoff
- 3-5 sample shipper request emails within Week 1
- Confirm Ascend TMS version (McLeod or InMotion Global) during Week 1

- Attend weekly 30-min stand-ups and exit review

**Huify responsibilities (Section 9):**
- Execute scope on Section 4 timeline

- Maintain same team (Josh, Ben, Erika), no handoff to customer success

## What it is

## Strategic thesis
**Bronson/Napoli was the proof-of-concept that earned Huify the right to pitch Hansen & Rosasco and every legal-vertical client that followed.** Napoli Shkolnik is a 250+ employee mass tort firm operating in NY and Puerto Rico, named in [[petroff-amshen-strategic-scoping-managing-partners]] reference list and [[petroff-amshen-marketing-content-operations]] as a reachable legal-vertical proof. Without this engagement, the Case Velocity framework, Black Box framing, and audit-to-retainer math have no enterprise-scale validation point.

The deeper move: **Bronson is the firm name used; Napoli Shkolnik is the underlying client.** "Bronson" appears as the operational sub-brand or team name. This naming convention shows up across the file structure ("Bronson - Mock Demo", "Bronson - Rosetta Stone", "Bronson Strategic Marketing Campaign Playbook"). Worth confirming with Josh whether Bronson is an internal name, an account name, or a partner-firm name within Napoli's ecosystem.

## What is interesting about this engagement
The file enumeration reveals an unusually rich workstream:

**Kickoff phase (Oct 2024):**
- Kickoff Meeting Agenda - Onboarding | Bronson | CS | Huify (2024-10-02) — the actual day one

body:
# Carpenter Chartered Cosell Playbook (with Zawad / HubSpot)

## What it is
Shared operating framework between Josh Harcus (Huify) and Zawad Ahmed (HubSpot Growth Specialist) for the Carpenter Chartered cosell. Dated 2026-04-24, v1.0, marked as living document updated after each joint call. Covers: deal state, weekly milestone cadence between now and target close (end of June 2026), lane split between HubSpot and Huify owners, attribution rules, prep/debrief rituals, named risk flags, and success vs stalling criteria. Includes the Friday May 1 call structure minute-by-minute.

## Strategic thesis
**HubSpot closes license cleanly. Huify closes services cleanly. The buyer gets one buying experience.** The playbook exists to prevent the two failure modes that kill partner cosells: (1) one party quoting across the other's lane in front of the customer, (2) one party contradicting the other in front of the customer. The hard rules section names both explicitly. Every other section flows from preserving those two rules.

The deeper strategic move: Phase 1 (initial license) is rep-sourced. HubSpot gets clean attribution. Phase 2 (expansion + services) is partner-sourced and Huify opens those deals. The partner relationship is monetized over time, not over a single transaction. This protects the long-term cosell flywheel.

## What is interesting about this doc
The lane-split table is the operational rigor that makes this playbook real. Each topic gets a Primary, a Supports, and (rarely) a Joint owner. There is no ambiguity on who quotes what. The "hard rules" section codifies the discipline:
1. Neither of us quotes across lanes in front of the customer. If asked something we don't own, the answer is "good question, let me let my counterpart scope that properly." No numbers in real time.
2. Neither of us contradicts the other in front of the customer. Nuance happens offline. We reframe jointly on the next call.
3. Neither of us collapses phases to close faster. Phased rollouts protect the buyer's risk tolerance and protect both attributions.

The prep-and-debrief ritual is the second piece of operational rigor: 10-minute prep sync 24-48 hours before every joint call, 5-bullet debrief within 4 hours after. Marked "Non negotiable. No exceptions even for a 15 minute check in." This is the discipline that prevents lane-split violations from accumulating.

The risk flags section is unusually candid for a sales playbook: no defined budget, no defined decision criteria, management committee not mapped, case management system unidentified, Sabina is a first-time buyer for this category, website redesign with outside studio may push competing CMS, compliance constraints unclear, no timeline anchor. Each risk has a named mitigation. This is the kind of risk disclosure that usually lives in someone's head; codifying it makes both parties more honest in the next prep sync.

The "deal is healthy when / deal is stalling when" pair on the success criteria section is the diagnostic any partner cosell should run weekly. Five healthy signals, five stalling signals, easy to score.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any partner cosell, channel partnership operating doc, or multi-party deal coordination:

1. **Lane split table** (Primary / Supports / Joint, with rep-sourced vs partner-sourced attribution explicitly named per deal phase). Drop into any cosell where two parties touch one customer.
2. **Three hard rules** (no cross-lane quote, no public contradiction, no phase collapse). Drop into any partner motion to prevent the two known failure modes.
3. **Prep-and-debrief ritual** (10 min before, 5 bullets within 4 hours after, non-negotiable). Drop into any high-stakes joint call cadence.
4. **Phase 1 license rep-sourced vs Phase 2 expansion partner-sourced attribution rule**. Drop into any HubSpot Partner cosell to prevent attribution disputes.
5. **Weekly milestone schedule from now to close** (by Friday May 1 / May 8 / May 15 / May 29). Drop into any deal where you want to compress time-to-close discipline.
6. **The Friday call minute-by-minute structure** (Zawad 5 / Josh 15 / Zawad 15 / Josh 10 / Joint 10 / Josh asks commitment question). Drop into any joint partner call agenda.
7. **The named commitment question** ("What would need to be true between now and May 15 for Carpenter to move forward?"). Drop into any first joint call closeout.
8. **Risk flags section format** (named risk + mitigation + watch-for signals). Drop into any sales playbook.
9. **Success vs Stalling criteria** (5 each, easy to score weekly). Drop into any deal health scorecard.
10. **Friday agenda template** (intros 5 / listening round per attendee 15 / HubSpot fit + tier walkthrough 15 / Case Velocity framework + reference 10 / MyCase scope + Phase 1 placement 10 / Q&A 10 / commitment ask + next steps 10). Drop into any first-meeting agenda for a multi-stakeholder buyer.
11. **Josh's intro for Zawad to deliver** (13 years HubSpot Partner, 100+ implementations, law firm focus, H&R reference, book authorship, ReadinessAudit.com). Drop into any partner motion as the partner's introduction script.

## ROI / outcome / story
**Target close dates:**
- Phase 1 license signed: end of June 2026
- Phase 1 services scope signed: within 2 weeks of license
- (Active deal value in [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]]: $150K HubSpot Implementation, Presentation Scheduled, 30%)

**What is working for us at time of playbook:**
1. HubSpot is presold at the tool level (Carpenter evaluated it internally before we showed up)
2. Sabina is a legitimate champion (conceded point solution sprawl + budgetless operation on first call)
3. CEO and COO both confirmed for next call (both need to be comfortable for this to move)
4. Close analog reference already built: Hansen & Rosasco (9/11 VCF firm, same shape as Carpenter)
5. Brand direction + compliance sensitivity understood (we know how to position so nothing gets rejected on tone)

**What is working against us:**
1. No defined marketing budget (firm still building annual number)
2. No defined decision criteria
3. Management committee named but not mapped (voting rule, meeting cadence, signing authority unknown)
4. Case management system unidentified (gating for integration scope) - resolved later as MyCase per [[carpenter-chartered-discovery-2026-05-05]]
5. Sabina is the first marketing person in firm history (org has no muscle for this kind of buying decision)
6. No timeline anchor yet (class action lawsuit event mentioned but not quantified)

**Expansion path named:**
1. Marketing Hub Pro (likely Phase 1)
2. Ops Hub Pro (Phase 2, enables Sabina's described automation)
3. Service Hub (post-launch, if client comm automation moves forward)

- **Operational sibling**: [[carpenter-chartered-discovery-2026-05-05]] is the May 5 discovery built off the Friday May 1 joint call defined here
- **Pre-call substantive prep**: [[carpenter-john-recommended-path]] (2026-05-07 1:1 prep) builds on this playbook's posture
- **Reference proof**: leans on [[hansen-rosasco-year-one-review-deck]] as the "9/11 Victim Compensation Fund firm with near-identical profile"
- **Channel motion**: this is the operational template for any future HubSpot Partner cosell (Patrick Maniego, Nicole Toler, Michila Dahlstrom, Shiv Shukla named in [[tortscale-readinessaudit-gtm-operating-plan-v2]] as other active partner relationships)

## Evolution
**Earlier**: Zawad opened the deal via HubSpot outbound, performed initial discovery. **This doc** (2026-04-24): v1.0 playbook published the week before the first joint call. **Phase 1 friday call**: 2026-05-01, joint discovery + HubSpot fit walkthrough + Case Velocity framework + commitment question. **Discovery deepening**: 2026-05-05 process discovery ([[carpenter-chartered-discovery-2026-05-05]]). **John 1:1**: 2026-05-07 ([[carpenter-john-recommended-path]]). **Target close**: end of June 2026 for Phase 1 license, +2 weeks for services scope. **Long arc**: Phase 2 expansion (Ops Hub Pro, Service Hub) partner-sourced and Huify-opened.

# Carpenter Chartered Process Discovery - May 5 2026

## What it is
The 60-minute joint working session plan for Carpenter Chartered's process discovery on 2026-05-05, 12pm ET. Structured as a department-by-department walk-through with 32 numbered questions across 7 sections, tracking "Discovery Completion: 42%" at meeting start (16 captured from prior calls and emails, 5 partial, 17 to capture live). Closes each department with the same anchor question: "What would you need from upstream to make John's vision real that you don't have today?" Ends with the gap-stacking exercise and Crawl/Walk/Run framing.

## Strategic thesis
**Make the firm describe itself to itself, in front of itself.** The format is built so that each department head walks their actual workflow on screen with everyone watching, then closes by naming what they need from upstream. By the time you reach Section 7 (stack the gaps), every person in the room has seen the others' gaps, which means the firm-wide picture is co-authored rather than imposed by Huify. The Crawl/Walk/Run framing at the end lets the room signal appetite without forcing a price discussion.

The deeper move: track "Discovery Completion %" explicitly. 42% before the meeting starts. The number shows the team that homework was done and signals what is still missing. It also gives Josh a quantitative artifact to present back in the proposal cover note.

## What is interesting about this doc
The "what would you need from upstream" question is the operational backbone. Asked of every department in the same form. Forces each lead to articulate dependencies, which surfaces the integration architecture without anyone having to draw the diagram explicitly. By the time Laura (case management) answers it, the room has already heard Sabina (marketing), Tammy (training), Carla (data), Haylee (intake), and Glenda (ops) describe what they need. The handoff design writes itself.

The Q24 question to Glenda is unusually sharp: "If we could give you 30% efficiency gain on intake and case admin, how would that change your hiring plans for the next 18 months?" This is the opportunity-cost discovery move that converts a soft "would be nice" into a quantifiable avoided-hire dollar value. It is the single question most likely to anchor the proposal economics.

The Q12 question on Tammy's training series is the opportunistic upsell discovery: VA accredited agent training market is $500-$3K per seat, Carpenter already runs 3 series/week with external participants, productizing this is a net-new revenue line. The question is framed for the room (not directly asked of Tammy) which is the right move because Tammy is not the decision-maker on a new revenue line, but John is in the room.

The "Carla, what's your role" question is honest about the gap in the prep email distribution: Carla was added but not introduced. Naming this upfront prevents the awkward "we should have known" moment.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any multi-stakeholder discovery, RevOps audit, or firm-wide CRM evaluation:

1. **Department-by-department walk-through structure** (each lead screen-shares their own workflow, watched by everyone). Drop into any firm-wide assessment.
2. **"What do you need from upstream" anchor question** (asked of every department in the same form, surfaces integration architecture by co-authorship). Drop into any discovery that touches multiple teams.
3. **Discovery Completion % tracking** (16 captured / 5 partial / 17 to capture live, visible at meeting start). Drop into any prep doc for a stakeholder meeting.
4. **Opportunity-cost question for the COO/CFO** ("If we gave you 30% efficiency gain, how would that change hiring plans for the next 18 months?"). Drop into any pricing-sensitive discovery.
5. **Stack-the-gaps closing move** (read back stacked gaps, get head-nod or pushback). Drop into any discovery closeout.
6. **Crawl/Walk/Run scope-signaling** without prices (let the room signal appetite). Drop into any pre-proposal commitment conversation.
7. **Productized-upsell framing question** (named market $500-$3K, current activity 3x/week, productizing = net new revenue + fixes Tammy's manual lift). Drop into any discovery where the firm is doing something adjacent that could be productized.
8. **Per-section progress meter** (section progress: 4/6 captured, 67%). Drop into any structured discovery plan.
9. **Live-vs-captured-vs-partial-vs-framed tags** on each question. Drop into any working discovery document where the same artifact gets updated live.
10. **The "anti-pattern" capture format** (Sabina: NOT patriotic flag-wave, NOT aggressive ads, NOT "stay top of mind" pings). Drop into any brand-positioning discovery.

## ROI / outcome / story
**Pre-meeting captured facts:**
- 17 -> 52 people in 5 years (3x headcount)
- 1,000 -> 2,500 active clients (2.5x caseload)
- Cases run 10-20 years per claim, 2-3 disabilities typical, sometimes 20-30 issues
- Lead volume disputed: 55-60/month inbound (Sabina recall) vs 155/month (Josh prep email cite); reconciliation needed in room
- Two intake leak modes already named: leads not returning communication, leads not submitting docs
- Class action growth: John won Godsey v. Wilkie and Wolfe v. Wilkie (first two class actions ever certified by US Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims). Aid and attendance claims rapidly growing.

**Josh's commitments coming out of the meeting:**
- Three-tier proposal (Crawl/Walk/Run) sent within 48 hours, anchored to the stacked gaps
- One-page recap of today's discovery, distributed to all attendees
- Carla's role formally captured
- Lead volume reconciliation closed in proposal cover note
- If warm: introduction between Sabina and Shannon Quinn at H&R for law-firm-marketing-lead peer call

**The strategic unlock:** John's class action data ask (pattern identification across 2,500 active clients) cannot be solved by spreadsheets. This is the use case that justifies HubSpot as the pattern layer on top of MyCase's case management. The discovery exists to surface this gap publicly so the proposal has a clean home.

## How this relates
- **Precursor to**: [[carpenter-john-recommended-path]] (the John 1:1 prep doc built 2026-05-07, two days after this discovery)
- **Operating layer**: [[carpenter-chartered-cosell-playbook]] (the HubSpot co-sell motion with Zawad)
- **Reference pattern**: explicitly leans on [[hansen-rosasco-year-one-review-deck]] as the proof anchor. Sabina-to-Shannon peer intro is the Bottom-Line Partner Series motion in microcosm
- **Vertical sibling**: similar shape to H&R (VA disability adjacent), confirms the pattern named in [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] for consumer-protection/VA-disability vertical
- **Tortscale parent plan**: this discovery is the inbound that feeds [[tortscale-readinessaudit-gtm-operating-plan-v2]] (Carpenter is the active Phase 1 deal target)
- **Champion**: Sabina Almeida (first marketing hire in firm history; 7 months in role)

## Evolution
**Earlier**: HubSpot already on Carpenter's internal shortlist before Sabina joined. Zawad opened the deal via HubSpot outbound and performed initial discovery. Josh introduced via [[carpenter-chartered-cosell-playbook]] (2026-04-24). Friday prep call already captured 16 of 32 discovery items. **This doc** (2026-05-05): the live working session. **Next**: 48-hour proposal, John 1:1 on 2026-05-07 ([[carpenter-john-recommended-path]]), Phase 1 close push named in [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]]. **Long arc**: Carpenter as candidate non-legal hero proof for [[huify-horizontal-expansion-gtm]] Phase 2 trigger.

## When to consult this in the future

# Carpenter Chartered - Recommended Path for John 1:1

## What it is
Sales prep doc for the 2026-05-07 1:30 ET call with John at Carpenter Chartered, a VA disability firm with ~2,500 active clients. Built the night before. Pairs with the HubSpot master brief (which sets meeting posture). Frames a Phase 1 offer at 6-8 weeks across HubSpot custom-object architecture, Freund class-action nurture, attribution dashboard, MyCase integration, and ongoing coaching.

## Strategic thesis
**Do not displace what works. Integrate what does not. Coach the team.** Carpenter is talking to multiple vendors. The pattern is to bet against the displacement pitch by giving the firm permission to keep what they already trust (MyCase for case management, Page for medical AI) and selling Huify as the integration plus engagement layer. This is the same wedge thinking used in [[huify-horizontal-expansion-gtm]] applied to a single deal context.

## What is interesting about this doc
The advisor-frame opener is the move worth studying: "This is informational. I am not asking you to commit tonight or Thursday. Sabina sent over the three areas; I built around those. If you find a better fit elsewhere, the framework still helps Carpenter decide." This explicitly disarms vendor-supplicant posture before it can form. Most B2B sales prep tries to control the call; this prep tries to release control and let the substance pull. The matched do-not-do list ("do not push pricing, do not ask for a signature, do not pretend they are not talking to other vendors") is the operational discipline that keeps the opener honest.

The second interesting move is the Crawl-Walk-Run artifact choice over the Plus One Subscription model. Crawl-Walk-Run was selected explicitly because the Subscription model "does not fit Carpenter cleanly." This is a reusable pattern: pick the artifact that matches the firm's risk profile, not the artifact you happen to have built recently.

## Reusable assets
Lift these out for future deals where Huify is going against a displacement pitch:

1. **Keep-what-works competitive matrix** (table contrasting Other HubSpot Partner / Filevine / Litify / Internal Hire vs Huify's keep-and-integrate posture). Drop in any deal where Filevine, Litify, or Clio is in the room.
2. **Three-areas response template** (responding directly to the buyer's stated areas instead of leading with Huify's own framework). Drop in any deal where the buyer has named what they want to see.
3. **Phase 1/2/3 timeline table** (6-8 weeks, then 3-6 months, then 6-12 months). Drop in any deal where the firm needs a multi-year roadmap but you only want commitment on Phase 1.

body:
# H&R AI Proof Extraction Plan

## What it is
The extraction blueprint (not the deck itself) for the year-one review deliverable to Hansen & Rosasco partners Dan Hansen and Troy Rosasco. Covers 2025-05-12 (signing) through 2026-05-18. Catalogs 18 verified shipped items, 5 suspected/unverified items, lists 30 specific screenshots to capture in a single ~90-min session, and proposes the deck structure.

## Strategic thesis
**Pair every claim with proof you can screenshot.** Dan and Troy are non-technical partners; the deck must make every shipped piece undeniable so the conversation moves from "did you build it" to "what's next." The pairing method (verbatim complaint quote -> what Huify built -> where it lives -> screenshot -> win in their language -> status) is the discipline. The deck is the artifact, the discipline is the asset.

The second strategic move is the AI-vs-not-AI ruthlessness. The doc explicitly defines what counts and what does not. Without that cut, every plumbing integration gets sold as "AI" and the deck loses credibility. With the cut, 18 verified items are real proof; the rest is plumbing that supports them.

## What is interesting about this doc
The PHANTOM section is the most useful piece of the document, even though it produces no deck content. Bree call summaries: flagged as phantom because no evidence exists in any system. Polly Call Sweep (vs Email Sweep): explicitly only Email Sweep is shipped. After-hours intake AI: pitched not built. These admissions stop the deck from rounding up and getting caught. The line "18 verified pieces beats 25 padded pieces" is the operational version of the discipline.

The other interesting move is the functional grouping (Option B) over chronological (Option A). Chronological feels like a journey but buries the strongest wins at the end (Polly, LCL). Functional opens each section with the complaint and lands the build directly against it, which lets Dan focus on Document AI (WD pain) and Troy on Attribution + Intake (his pain) without losing the through-line.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any client year-end review, milestone deck, or hero-story extraction:

1. **Pairing template** (5 fields: verbatim quote, what we built, where it lives, screenshot to capture, win in their language, status). This is the most reusable artifact in the doc. Drop it into any client retro.
2. **AI-vs-not-AI definition cut** (counts as AI: LLM features, workflow automations that replaced judgment, agentic task creation; does not count: plain integrations, SOPs, custom views, email templates without sequencing, property creation). Drop into any AI-adjacent deck.
3. **Source scan table** (HubSpot / Pandadoc / Gong / Asana / Slack / Gmail / Vidyard / HubSpot Documents Library; what to look for + how to extract + what is NOT in scope per source). Drop into any extraction exercise across an integrated stack.
4. **Anti-pattern catalog for proof decks** (internal Huify metrics, tech stack diagrams, future-state beyond closing, anything not adopted, anything not screenshottable, the Phantom Section, plumbing on its own). Drop into any client-facing deliverable.
5. **Punch list before deck build** (verify still-live, confirm adoption counts, check sandbox state). Drop into any deliverable that depends on shipped infrastructure.
6. **Functional vs chronological deck structure decision** (with the explicit tradeoff articulated). Drop into any milestone storytelling exercise.

## ROI / outcome / story
This is the year-1 proof artifact behind the largest active Huify engagement. Coverage window 2025-05-12 to 2026-05-18. Specific shipped wins with measurable outcomes:

- **LCL Phase 1 (Loss Calculation Letter)**: a letter that took Kim 30+ minutes per claim now auto-generates 85% of the way there. Kim's time goes to exceptions, not typing.
- **Polly Email Sweep (agentic staffer)**: confirmed by tagged Asana tasks throughout April-May 2026. Auto-creates tasks from inbound emails with confidence scores and source quotes.
- **Pandadoc 32-template migration**: clients now get packets with the right name and right VCF number every time. Solves a documented wrong-info-in-packets failure mode.
- **CallRail source workflow**: Shannon Quinn's marketing numbers are right without her touching them. Replaces manual source patching.
- **Leadership dashboard email**: Dan + Troy + Sam now get pipeline health in their inbox every Monday without logging in.
- **Inactive-claim follow-up**: no claim sits idle 60+ days without case manager being told.
- **Required-fields gate**: pipeline now enforces data quality at stage transitions.
- **Huify Documents platform**: custom-built app (Ben Riordan), not bolted-on third-party tool. API v1 shipped 4/19/2026, HubSpot extension live.

The hero quote pattern: every win restated in their language ("Faster intake calls, fewer typos, no more screen sheets on a clipboard" / "WD retainers generate clean every time" / "Every client call lives on the client's record"). These quotes are reusable for future case studies, sales decks, and the horizontal expansion proof rail in [[huify-horizontal-expansion-gtm]].

## How this relates
- **Wedge proof source**: This is THE Hansen story that [[huify-horizontal-expansion-gtm]] uses as the wedge anchor. Without this year-1 outcome, the horizontal expansion play has no proof
- **Feeds the referral motion**: Every shipped item in this catalog is potential referral-ask language ("we helped Hansen & Rosasco untangle their attribution and intake")
- **Pattern parent**: The pairing method here is the precursor to any future client retrospective Huify produces
- **Adjacent deals**: [[carpenter-john-recommended-path]] references this story explicitly as proof; future deals will too

## Evolution
**Earlier**: signing 2025-05-12, Onboarding Kickoff 5/12/2025 (Sam Stone), Team Training & Playbook Launch 6/3/2025 (Greg Rosasco), follow-up call 6/11/2025 (Troy Rosasco). **Mid-stream**: workflows shipped April-May 2026 (Sergio), Pandadoc migration April-May 2026 (Erika), Document AI 2026-04 forward (Ben). **This doc** (2026-05-19): the extraction blueprint that turns 12 months of work into the year-one review artifact. **Next**: deck build, partner review meeting with Dan and Troy, decision on Phase 2 scope (Polly Call Sweep, LCL Phase 2 AI, retainer auto-parsing). **Long arc**: if year-1 lands well, Hansen becomes a multi-year reference and the candidate non-legal hero list in [[huify-horizontal-expansion-gtm]] gets unlocked once a second hero is confirmed.

## When to consult this in the future
- Preparing a year-end or milestone review for any client
- Extracting hero-story material for a new sales deck or landing page
- Coaching the team on the pairing-method discipline
- Defining what counts as "AI" in any client-facing artifact
- Building a punch list before shipping a deliverable that depends on live infrastructure
- Choosing between chronological and functional storytelling for a complex multi-quarter engagement

## Caveats / what is NOT in this doc
The doc is the extraction blueprint, not the deck. Dollar outcomes are referenced indirectly via wins but no aggregate $ amount is stated. Adoption rates are flagged as needing verification (LCL Phase 1 under 10 real claims processed = framing changes to "ready to scale"). The audience scope decision (Dan+Troy only vs Dan+Troy+Sam) is still open and changes which wins get more weight.

body:
# Hansen & Rosasco Year One Review (12-slide deck)

## What it is
The actual 12-slide year-one review presentation for Dan Hansen and Troy Rosasco, dated May 2026. The shipped artifact, not the blueprint (the blueprint lives in [[hansen-rosasco-ai-proof-extraction-plan]]). Opens with the Black Box problem frame, walks through what was built across four AI pillars (Intake, Attribution, Document, Communication), lands the $526K capacity-recovered number, and closes with a named ask: approve H&R as the named reference case for Huify's 2026 plaintiff-firm launch.

## Strategic thesis
**Frame the problem in their language first, then show every shipped piece as a direct answer to it.** Slide 2 establishes The Black Box ("Marketing dollars go in. Some retained cases come out. Nobody can draw the line between them"). Every subsequent slide ties back to that frame. The deck does not pitch Huify, it pitches the firm's own transformation. The big number ($526K operational capacity recovered) is the bridge between the proof and the ask.

The deeper move: durability framing on slide 10 ("Institutional knowledge no longer lives in any one person's head. Whoever sits in the seat next, the firm keeps moving") flips the standard consulting fear ("what happens when the consultant leaves") into a partner's selling point.

## What is interesting about this doc
The Black Box frame is the most reusable strategic asset Huify owns. It works because it does not require the partner to admit fault. "Every plaintiff firm has a Black Box" externalizes the problem before naming it inside H&R. That single rhetorical move is the reason the deck opens without defense.

The four-pillar grouping (Intake AI / Attribution AI / Document AI / Communication AI) is the operational categorization that the blueprint debated (functional vs chronological) and chose. The deck demonstrates that the functional grouping works: each pillar gets a slide with shipped wins, and Dan or Troy can drop into the pillar that matches their pain (Dan into Document, Troy into Attribution + Intake).

The named ask is unusually clean: three specific deliverables (publish the $526K story, review every public asset before it ships, co-sign one joint piece). No vague "deepen the relationship" language. The ask is a contract for what reference-case status means.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any client retrospective, hero-deck build, or reference-case ask:

1. **Black Box problem frame** (visual: marketing dollars in -> question marks -> retained cases out). Drop into any plaintiff-firm pitch, or rewire for any vertical with attribution opacity (SaaS PLG funnels, agency referral chaos, manufacturing channel mix).
2. **Before/After pairing for documents** (slide 8 shows the manual copy-paste process step by step, then the auto-generated alternative). Drop into any deliverable that proves automation by showing the manual alternative in painful detail.
3. **Four-pillar AI grouping** (Intake, Attribution, Document, Communication). Drop into any client-facing deck where you need to organize multiple AI/automation pieces. Reusable taxonomy.
4. **Durability slide template** (THE SYSTEM CARRIES list vs PEOPLE STILL OWN list). Drop into any consulting deliverable to neutralize the "what happens when you leave" question.
5. **Named-ask close** (3 specific items, not vague relationship-building). Drop into any reference-case ask, partnership ask, or expansion ask.
6. **"The Number" single-slide reveal** ($526K with the methodology promised in appendix). Drop into any milestone deck where you have one outcome number that earns its own slide.

## ROI / outcome / story
**The Hero Numbers:**
- **$1.08M** in annual marketing spend now visible per-channel per-month and tied to retained cases (replaces Shannon's spreadsheet and three reports nobody trusted)
- **$526K** operational capacity recovered in year one (hours saved, leads recovered, errors eliminated; methodology in appendix, backing math pending Josh verification)
- **23,000+** claim records migrated and audited (zero claims lost in LawRuler-to-HubSpot move)
- **6+ months** of custom build, not a SaaS install
- **31 templates** rebuilt to new variable map
- **~12K records** auto-mapped through status remediation
- **20 manual letters per week, 15 min each** as the lower bound on what LCL document automation returns

**The Story Arc:**
- Starting line (slide 3): LawRuler creaking under volume, no per-channel attribution, intake follow-up in spreadsheets and heads, leadership flying blind
- What we built (slide 4): three systems (Intake, Case Management, Document) on a M0-to-M12 timeline
- What we installed (slide 5): four AI pillars with named features (Breeze AI summaries, WTCHP sequences, status remediation; per-channel attribution + cost-per-signed-case + 10% fee forecast; PandaDoc variable sync + 31 templates rebuilt + LCL Phase 1; RingCentral transcription + auto-logged calls)
- What is next (slide 11): three workstreams already moving (LCL AI document automation Phase 2, Witness Presence Statement cross-check Phase 3, attribution deeper layer)
- The ask (slide 12): named reference case + 3 deliverables

**The Reusable Quote Material:**
- "Every plaintiff firm has a Black Box"
- "We built the operating system for a 9/11 VCF practice. Not configured. Not templated. Custom-built end to end."
- "Agentic AI lives inside the work. Not a separate tool. Not a chatbot."
- "Intake runs on the system, not on memory."
- "The team stopped retyping."
- "Institutional knowledge no longer lives in any one person's head."

## How this relates
- **Blueprint parent**: [[hansen-rosasco-ai-proof-extraction-plan]] is the extraction blueprint that produced this deck. The 18 verified shipped items in the blueprint condense into the four-pillar story here
- **Asset pillar for expansion**: [[huify-horizontal-expansion-gtm]] explicitly leans on this story as the wedge anchor. The $526K and the "we built the operating system" framing become the referral-ask language
- **Direct sales feeder**: [[carpenter-john-recommended-path]] uses the H&R outcome as competitive proof against Filevine, Litify, and internal-hire pitches
- **GTM v2 anchor**: [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] names the H&R Bottom-Line Partner Series as a real channel (3-5 co-branded case studies with H&R's vendor partners). The deck's named ask (co-sign one joint piece) is the operational unlock for that channel
- **Methodology lineage**: the Black Box frame is the most-reused strategic asset Huify owns; expect it to appear in every vertical landing page and pitch

## Evolution
**Earlier**: signing 2025-05-12, 23K records migrated zero lost, four AI pillars built across 12 months. **Blueprint**: [[hansen-rosasco-ai-proof-extraction-plan]] extracted 18 verified pieces with verbatim quotes and screenshot paths. **This doc** (2026-05-19): the actual 12-slide presentation, condensed to four pillars, ready for partner review. **Next**: deliver to Dan and Troy (Josh to verify $526K backing math first), get reference-case approval, unlock H&R Bottom-Line Partner Series production. **Long arc**: H&R as named reference case in 2026 plaintiff-firm launch -> story becomes the proof rail for [[huify-horizontal-expansion-gtm]] -> if Phase 2 triggers, a second hero (Carpenter, Mediafly, or other) joins H&R.

## When to consult this in the future
- Building a year-end review or milestone deck for any client
- Looking for the Black Box framing template to adapt to another vertical
- Sourcing hero quotes for a sales deck or landing page
- Demonstrating durability framing (system vs people) for a consulting engagement
- Writing a named ask for reference-case status or co-marketing collaboration
- Recalling the four-pillar AI taxonomy

## Caveats
The $526K capacity-recovered figure has a "Josh to verify backing math before final print" flag on slide 9. Same flag on the staff-time-recovered figure on slide 8. Both numbers anchor the deck; verification is gating to print. Slide 12's ask is named but not yet accepted by Dan and Troy.
