body:
# Huify Horizontal Expansion GTM

## What it is
Strategy brief authored 2026-05-18 (status: pre-decision, assets pending greenlight) for whether and how Huify should expand beyond the legal vertical proof point (Hansen & Rosasco) into other professional services verticals. Frames four options (parallel verticals, umbrella offer, sequential rollout, referral-only) and lands on a hybrid: run the referral motion across the entire warm list in Week 1 using the H&R story, hold the dedicated non-legal landing page until a milestone trigger fires.

## Strategic thesis
**Sharp wedge plus low-cost referral plus gated horizontal expansion.** ReadinessAudit.com/legal is the highest-converting URL in the stack right now and the wedge is narrow on purpose. Diluting it with horizontal copy costs 30-50% on legal conversion. The play is to protect the wedge while still monetizing the non-legal warm list through a near-zero-cost referral ask, then only build a second vertical landing page after explicit proof signals fire (3 LRSAs booked AND 1+ "this sounds like my business" reply from non-legal).

The deeper bet: the warm list is a depreciating asset. Every quarter a warm contact stays cold, willingness to re-engage decays. Referral motion captures the upside without forcing Huify into premature horizontal positioning.

## What is interesting about this doc
The four-option analysis lands on D+C hybrid, not on the "obvious" pure D (referral only) or pure C (sequential). Pure referral leaves money on the table for any non-legal contact who actually has the same Black Box pain in their own business. Pure sequential parks the warm list for 90 days. The hybrid is the move most people would not pick because it requires holding two thoughts (protect the wedge AND monetize the warm list) without collapsing one into the other.

The smallest-viable-experiment design is also worth studying: 4 LinkedIn posts over 4 weeks, no landing page, no new offer, just translate the Hansen story into 4 different non-legal vertical pains. Kill criteria are explicit (under 3 qualified replies = abandon horizontal, 7+ = green light Phase 2). Cost: 4 hours of Josh's writing time per week, zero paid spend. This is the cheapest possible validation move and it should be the default pattern for any future vertical decision.

The third interesting move: no monetary referral incentive on the warm list. The argument is that the warm list is a relationship list, not an affiliate list, and paying for intros cheapens the relationship. Exception carved out for HubSpot AE/partner segment (different relationship type, different motion, different contract).

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any future vertical decision, GTM scope choice, or warm-list activation:

1. **Four-options decision frame** (parallel verticals / umbrella / sequential / referral-only) with explicit pros and cons. Drop into any expansion-scope decision.
2. **Milestone-gated expansion trigger** (specific binary criteria that must fire before Phase 2 launches). Drop into any phased rollout where you want to avoid premature scaling.
3. **Smallest-viable-experiment template** (1 post/week, 4 weeks, defined kill/proceed criteria, zero new assets). Drop into any validation question that does not need infrastructure to test.
4. **Clean-ask referral motion** (email template + LinkedIn DM template + tracking URL pattern + 30/60 day follow-up cadence + reply-to-unsubscribe ratio kill criterion). Drop into any warm-list referral activation.
5. **Segmentation map template** (Industry filter -> Segment -> Treatment -> Primary CTA -> Asset divergence). Drop into any HubSpot list-segmentation decision.
6. **Asset divergence vs reuse matrix** (where assets diverge: landing page hero copy, Loom, hero quote; where they share: audit methodology, deliverable structure, sales motion, tracking schema, brand). Drop into any multi-vertical or multi-segment asset planning.
7. **Sub-vertical pick-one rule** (do not launch Phase 2 with a generic "pro services" page; pick the sub-vertical with the strongest second hero candidate, or do not launch). Drop into any horizontal expansion conversation.
8. **No-paid-referral logic with partner-tier exception** (when to keep ask clean vs when to structure a partner commission). Drop into any partner-program design.

## ROI hook / story angle
Pre-outcome. This is the brief that decides the 90-day motion, not a reported result. Forward-looking outcomes that matter:

- **If D+C hybrid is greenlit**: warm list gets activated in Week 1 at near-zero asset cost. Legal LRSA volume tracks normally. Tracking infrastructure (UTM + HubSpot workflow) becomes the audit trail for which warm contacts are friend-of-firm vs "this is me too."
- **If Phase 2 triggers**: ReadinessAudit.com/[sub-vertical] launches with ~7 new assets, same audit methodology, same retainer SKU on the back end. Net new revenue from a second vertical without diluting legal.
- **If Phase 2 does not trigger**: validates that the legal wedge is the right and only wedge for now. Time saved goes to deepening legal motion. Not a failure, it is data.

Anchor proof: the Hansen & Rosasco year-one outcome ([[hansen-rosasco-ai-proof-extraction-plan]]) is the asset the entire referral ask leans on. The H&R quote ("Hüify is doing focused plaintiff-firm work right now and Hansen & Rosasco was our hero outcome") is reusable verbatim across email, LinkedIn DM, and partner-AE asks.

## How this relates
- **Proof source**: depends entirely on [[hansen-rosasco-ai-proof-extraction-plan]] as the wedge anchor. No H&R story = no warm-list ask = no Phase 2 trigger possible
- **Active deal feeder**: [[carpenter-john-recommended-path]] is one of the candidate non-legal hero stories named in this doc. If Carpenter signs and produces an outcome, it unlocks Phase 2
- **Other candidate heroes**: Mediafly ([[mediafly-sizzle-deck]]), EnSight, Plus One. All need Josh validation before any can become Phase 2 hero
- **Sibling brand frame**: keep-what-works thinking in [[carpenter-john-recommended-path]] is the deal-level expression of the same don't-displace-the-wedge logic at the brand level
- **Tracking infra**: depends on existing HubSpot warm list, CallRail attribution, UTM schema, ReadinessAudit.com domain authority

## Evolution
**Earlier**: Hansen & Rosasco signing (2025-05-12) and year-one outcome (proven by [[hansen-rosasco-ai-proof-extraction-plan]]) created the wedge proof. Earlier GTM thinking lives in [[huify-gtm-writeup]] and [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] and [[huify-gtm-context-compilation]]. **This doc** (2026-05-19): the expansion decision document, builds on the Hansen proof and the existing audit funnel. **Next**: Josh decides five binary items (root page routing, Week 1 send, paid vs clean, parallel LinkedIn, Phase 2 sub-vertical). **Long arc**: if Phase 2 triggers, Huify becomes a dual-vertical firm. If it does not, the firm goes deeper on legal and the warm-list referral motion becomes the durable activation pattern.

## When to consult this in the future
- Considering whether to expand into a new vertical or stay narrow
- Deciding between parallel, umbrella, sequential, or referral-only expansion patterns
- Designing a warm-list referral motion (clean ask vs paid incentive question)
- Planning a milestone-gated launch where you want to avoid premature scaling
- Running a smallest-viable-experiment to validate a market segment without building infrastructure
- Segmenting a HubSpot list for a multi-segment campaign
- Choosing a sub-vertical for a new landing page

## Open decisions for Josh (5 binary items)
1. Lock ReadinessAudit.com root as vertical-neutral with two-button choice (recommended) vs redirect to /legal
2. Send referral ask in Week 1 (recommended) vs wait for 3 legal LRSAs
3. Clean referral ask (recommended for warm list) vs paid incentive
4. LinkedIn horizontal experiment in parallel (recommended) vs sequential
5. Phase 2 sub-vertical (agency vs consulting vs generic pro-services - generic NOT recommended)

## Open data items
HubSpot contact counts by Industry filter, lifecycle stage breakdown, engagement recency distribution, non-legal hero story validation (Mediafly / Carpenter / EnSight / Plus One), ReadinessAudit.com root traffic / SEO authority baseline.

# Hüify Skills + Scheduled Tasks Analysis

## What it is
Operational audit dated 2026-05-06, inventorying every scheduled Claude skill Huify actually runs day-to-day: 8 enabled, 5 disabled, 2 behavioral (non-scheduled). Built explicitly as source data for the Mediafly Plus One conversation and a permanent reference for productizing the motion. Notes which skills survived iteration, which got consolidated, and what patterns hold. Closes with the recommended 3-skill starter pack any sales org should roll out first.

## Strategic thesis
**Consolidation beats single-purpose.** The five disabled skills were all absorbed into broader sweeps. Lesson: do not ship six narrow skills when one well-scoped sweep covers the same ground. The team adopts the broad sweep and forgets the narrow ones.

The deeper move is **ground truth, not pitch**: Huify runs Plus One on itself. The proof that "skill-as-a-service plus coaching retainer" works is not in a deck, it is in this audit. The Mediafly sales motion ([[mediafly-sizzle-deck]]) leans on this document as the credibility anchor. Eight skills running, 4×/day on the highest-frequency one, 5 earlier narrow skills consolidated.

## What is interesting about this doc
The frequency distribution is the most useful operational signal Huify has. Top three skills (daily-gong-coaching ~16 runs/wk, post-meeting-hubspot-tasks ~12 runs/wk, inbox-and-pipeline-sweep 15 runs/wk) all operate on the call/meeting/inbox loop. That is where automation earns its keep. Everything else is weekly or monthly.

The single most important strategic insight named in the doc: **day-of-meeting-prep is the door any sales-team rollout should open first because they are already standing at it.** AEs already use AI for call prep. Every other gap is manual. Lead with the skill that extends what they already trust, then earn the right to deeper write-back permissions.

The consolidation pattern (five narrow skills absorbed into broader sweeps) is the operational law of skill design at Huify. It directly informs the Mediafly pitch: "we tried five narrow things first, they all got absorbed, so for you we are starting with the broad one."

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any sales-ops automation, productized-services design, or skill-rollout motion:

1. **The 8-skill inventory itself** (day-of-meeting-prep, inbox-and-pipeline-sweep, post-meeting-hubspot-tasks, daily-gong-coaching, monday-crm-hygiene, weekly-pipeline-review, l10-issue-sweep, monthly-crm-health). Drop into any client kickoff as the "here is what good looks like" reference set.
2. **The 3-skill starter pack** (Pre-call deal prep, Post-call CRM logging, Async call coaching) with explicit deployment order. Drop into any new sales-org rollout.
3. **The disabled-skills lesson** (5 narrow skills consolidated into broader sweeps). Drop into any skill-design conversation to prevent over-narrow proposals.
4. **Day-of-meeting-prep playbook** (weekday 7am, reads calendar, posts to Slack, every meeting prepped). The proven entry point.
5. **Daily-gong-coaching pattern** (4×/day Tue-Fri, no Mondays because calls happen Tue-Fri). Drop into any call-coaching-as-a-service design.
6. **L10-issue-sweep pattern** (Tuesday 10am, pre-meeting, drafts staged for approval before pushing to Notion). Drop into any pre-meeting prep automation where human approval gates writes.
7. **Approve-to-write progression** (month 1 read-only, month 2 approve-to-write). Drop into any client motion where the client's CRM admin needs to gain trust before allowing autonomous writes.
8. **Frequency distribution as adoption signal** (top 3 = call/meeting/inbox loop). Drop into any AI-adoption diagnostic.
9. **Latent skill candidates pattern** (look at session-title patterns for recurring manual work). Drop into any audit of where to invest skill-build effort.
10. **Brain-sync + advisor-frame as behavioral skills** (non-scheduled, shape every session). Drop into any agentic system that needs persistent behavior shaping.

## ROI / outcome / story
**Operational facts as story-units:**
- 8 scheduled skills running automatically at Huify
- 5 earlier narrow skills built and consolidated (proof of iteration)
- daily-gong-coaching runs ~16x/week (Tue-Fri, 4x/day)
- post-meeting-hubspot-tasks runs ~12x/week (Tue-Thu, 4x/day)
- inbox-and-pipeline-sweep runs 15x/week (weekdays, 3x/day)
- day-of-meeting-prep runs 5x/week (every weekday 7am, the one nobody asks to turn off)
- 2 behavioral skills (brain-sync, advisor-frame) shape every session

**Plus One ROI math (from sibling deck):**
- 10 AEs × 8 calls/week × 25 min × 4 weeks = 133 hrs saved per month
- At $95/hr fully-loaded AE cost = $12,635 monthly value
- vs $6K/month Plus One subscription = 2.1× conservative ROI
- 3-5× with forecast accuracy lift, deal velocity, skill-library compounding

**Customer-voice line ready for Mediafly conversation:**
"You can fumble your way to build these things, but what you bring is that you can help it be live tomorrow with guardrails." (Lee Roquet)

## How this relates
- **Sales asset parent**: feeds [[mediafly-sizzle-deck]] directly. Every claim in the deck ("8 skills running," "4x/day cadence," "5 earlier consolidated") comes from this audit
- **Productized motion source**: Plus One Subscription packaging in [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] depends on this audit existing
- **Operational footprint of**: [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] (this is how Huify itself executes the GTM)

- **Recurring-pattern source**: latent skill candidates (proposal/one-pager builder, strategic deal prep, champion management tracker, proposal-to-SOW converter, daily Forge sync) are the candidate build list for next-build sequencing

## Evolution
**Earlier**: 13 skills built over time, 5 disabled because absorbed into broader sweeps. **This doc** (2026-05-06): the audit moment, captured for Mediafly conversation. **Recently built (not yet scheduled)**: brain-sync (federates josh-identity across Claude accounts), advisor-frame (strips vendor-supplicant language). **Next**: build the proposal/one-pager builder skill (top candidate) and the strategic-deal-prep skill (second candidate). **Long arc**: this audit becomes the recurring quarterly artifact that drives the productized-skills roadmap and the Plus One sales motion.

body:
# Mediafly Plus One Sizzle Deck

## What it is
10-slide sales pitch for Mediafly's Lee Roquet, dated May 2026. Productizes Huify's internal skills motion ("8 skills running on automated cadence at Hüify right now") into a saleable subscription called Plus One. Frames Huify as trusted advisor not vendor, sells skill-as-a-service plus coaching retainer, locks Mediafly as one of three founding-customer slots. Three lanes: $3K Launch (one skill, under 7 days), $6K/4-weeks Standard auto-renew (one new skill/month + advisory), $3K/week High-Cadence (full team transformation in a quarter). Cancel anytime. IP transfers to Mediafly the day each skill ships.

## Strategic thesis
**Open one door, you've got them all.** Mediafly's AEs already use AI for one thing: pre-call prep. The pitch frames the Pre-call deal prep agent as the door they are already standing at, then maps the next six months as compounding skills (forecast hygiene, post-call summary with approve-to-write, customer health monitor, win/loss agent, pipeline review automation). Each new skill opens a new department: sales -> CS -> RevOps.

The deeper strategic move is **ground truth, not pitch.** Slide 8 establishes "we run this on ourselves, every day" with the same 8/4×/5 numbers from [[huify-skills-scheduled-tasks-analysis]]. The proof is operational fact, not marketing claim. Plus One is "our operations playbook turned into your platform."

Third strategic move: **Hüify takes the risk.** Cancel anytime no notice, IP transfers immediately, $3K launch sits below discretionary spend caps (no CFO approval needed), founding customer rate locked for life. Every objection neutralized in slide 9 before it can form.

## What is interesting about this doc
The $3K launch price as a deliberate move below discretionary spend caps is the single most underrated tactic in this deck. No CFO approval = no procurement cycle = decision can be made on the call. Combined with cancel-anytime + IP-transfers, the buyer's risk surface is reduced to "is the first skill worth $3K." That is a near-impossible price point to defend against.

The Salesforce + Agentforce timing frame on slide 2 is the second sharp move: "Agentforce builds take 6 to 8 weeks. Plus One ships skill one in 7 days." This positions Huify against the dominant Salesforce-native option without naming it as a competitor. The buyer self-selects on speed-to-live.

The Lee-personally section on slide 9 is the third interesting move: "Personal-use license follows you. If you leave Mediafly, the skill keeps working in your hands." This converts the buyer from a corporate decision-maker into a personal beneficiary. Founding customer reference status across the productized motion + co-author position on the case study and product roadmap aligns Lee's career narrative with Huify's product roadmap. Sale becomes mutual investment, not vendor selection.

The "approve-to-write progression" (month 1 read-only, month 2 approve-to-write, then full SF write-back) is a clean operational unlock for the most-feared objection ("we cannot let an AI write to our CRM"). Phased trust = phased permissions.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any productized-services sales motion, founding-customer offer, or sales-ops automation pitch:

1. **Three-lane offer structure** (Launch / Standard auto-renew / High-Cadence). One commitment, buyer chooses cadence. Drop into any productized subscription motion.
2. **$3K launch price below discretionary spend caps** (no CFO approval, no procurement cycle, decision on the call). Drop into any motion where you want to land the first wedge below approval thresholds.
3. **Founding customer rate locked for life** (three slots, time-bounded scarcity, lifetime price guarantee). Drop into any productized motion where you need to compress initial deal cycle.
4. **Cancel-anytime + IP-transfers + personal-use license** (three risk-reversals stacked). Drop into any motion where buyer risk is the main objection.
5. **Ground-truth-not-pitch operational slide** (we run this on ourselves, here are the numbers: 8/4×/5). Drop into any pitch where the seller is also a heavy user of the product.
6. **Six-month skill compounding roadmap** (1 skill/month with department expansion: Sales month 1-3, CS month 4, RevOps month 5, pipeline-review automation month 6). Drop into any productized-services motion that needs a believable expansion narrative.
7. **Door-already-standing-at framing** (start with the skill that extends what they already trust). Drop into any AI rollout where adoption velocity is the constraint.
8. **Approve-to-write progression** (read-only month 1, approve-to-write month 2). Drop into any CRM-write-back motion where admin trust is the gating concern.
9. **Lee-personally section** (personal-use license + leadership readout deck + reference status + co-author position). Drop into any deal where you need the champion's career narrative aligned with your product roadmap.
10. **Agentforce-comparison frame** ("their build = 6-8 weeks, ours = 7 days") without naming the competitor as competitor. Drop into any motion against a slower platform-native alternative.
11. **The ROI math format** (subscription cost / saved time / fully-loaded rate / monthly value / ratio). 25 min/call × 8 calls/wk × 10 AEs × 4 wks = 133 hrs at $95/hr = $12,635 vs $6K = 2.1× conservative. Drop into any sales-ops productivity pitch.

## ROI / outcome / story
**The conservative math (slide 7):**
- Standard subscription: $6,000 every 4 weeks
- AE time saved per call (pre-call prep + post-call admin): 25 minutes
- 10 AEs × 8 calls/week × 25 min × 4 weeks = 133 hrs/month saved
- Fully-loaded AE cost/hour: $95
- Monthly value of recovered AE time: $12,635
- Net monthly ROI: 2.1×

**The realistic math (with compounding):**
3-5× ROI when adding forecast accuracy lift, deal velocity from cleaner pipeline, and skill-library compounding ("skills you build month one keep delivering month twelve").

**The six-month outcome story (slide 5):**
- Month 1: Pre-call deal prep agent shipped, AE adoption inside 2 weeks
- Month 2: Forecast hygiene flag, quarterly board credit on forecast accuracy
- Month 3: Post-call summary with approve-to-write, SF write-back access earned
- Month 4: CS door opens (customer health monitor)
- Month 5: RevOps door opens (win/loss analysis agent)
- Month 6: Pipeline review automation replaces a weekly meeting

**The deal value:**
$3K launch + ~$72K-78K/year on Standard auto-renew = ~$75K-81K Year 1 ACV. Open Mediafly pipeline value in [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]]: $75K Presentation Scheduled at 30%.

## How this relates
- **Operational truth source**: every claim in this deck comes from [[huify-skills-scheduled-tasks-analysis]]. The 8 skills, the 4×/day cadence, the 5 consolidated narrow skills are all factual statements grounded there
- **GTM v2 active deal**: named in [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] open pipeline ($75K Presentation Scheduled, 30%, Phase 1 close push)
- **Plus One Subscription**: this is the product. Same model named in v2 Bet 4 as a separate motion from the audit-to-retainer engine
- **Champion node**: Lee Roquet is the named champion. The Lee-personally section converts him from gatekeeper to co-author
- **Vertical parallel**: Mediafly is the SaaS-sales-ops vertical proof candidate; H&R is the legal vertical proof; Carpenter is the consumer-protection/VA-disability candidate
- **Frameworks shared**: founding-customer-rate, three-lane-offer, ground-truth-not-pitch are all reusable across other Plus One pitches (next prospects: any Series B+ SaaS sales org)

## Evolution
**Earlier**: Huify built 8 scheduled skills internally over months. 5 narrow skills consolidated into broader sweeps. Lee Roquet conversation revealed Mediafly already uses AI for pre-call prep only. Lee framed the ask as "skill-as-a-service plus coaching retainer." **This doc** (2026-05-06): the 10-slide pitch shipped after that conversation. **Next**: Mediafly decision, founding-customer commit or pass. **Long arc**: if Mediafly signs, Plus One becomes a productized motion with three founding customers shaping the product roadmap. Mediafly becomes the SaaS-sales-ops hero proof point for [[huify-horizontal-expansion-gtm]] Phase 2 trigger.

## When to consult this in the future

## Strategic thesis
**You bought the platform, now make it pay.** Petroff Amshen is paying for Marketing Hub Pro and Content Hub Pro monthly with neither hub producing measurable revenue. The website is on Webflow. Drip campaigns at zero. Remarketing at zero. ~110 LPs scattered. Ad spend on Google, Meta, TikTok without clean attribution to retainers. "That is not a HubSpot problem. The platform works. The gap is between what HubSpot can do and what is currently configured."

The deeper strategic move: **bundle the audit into Phase 1A instead of selling it separately.** Most agencies sell a discovery audit as a separate engagement before any building happens. This doc explicitly does not. The site inventory, URL consolidation map, and Phase 2 migration scoping all happen during Phase 1A as part of the work. The buyer gets the audit deliverables AND the working marketing engine in the same engagement, on the same timeline, at no separate cost.

The third move: **Closing Culture brand framing**. "Most HubSpot Solutions Partners are configuration shops. We are a conversion shop that uses HubSpot." The brand is the literal title of Josh's book ("A Closing Culture: How to Build a Sales-Driven Organization That Closes More Deals"). Every engagement structured around what produces signed retainers, not what looks good on a dashboard. This is the positioning anchor.

## What is interesting about this doc
The cost-of-inaction analysis is the rhetorical move that anchors the math. Three sourced industry benchmarks (legal LP conversion 3.4% avg / 6.3% median, paid media waste 15-25% in B2C legal, lead recovery 5-12% with drip+remarketing) stack into a quantified gap. The reader is doing the math against their own firm before the pricing table arrives.

The "Three things that means for Petroff Amshen" framing (conversion-first engineering, law firm specialization, honest scope) is the proof structure. Each gets one paragraph. Conversion-first engineering names the methodology and the conservative math. Law firm specialization names three recent legal builds (Napoli Shkolnik 250+ employees NY+PR mass tort, Hansen & Rosasco NYC foreclosure + 9/11 claims, a separate 9/11 claims firm) with case-size range ($5K to $500K+ average retainer). Honest scope explicitly names what we do NOT do (run your ads, replace IOLA, write your blog posts) which is the credibility move.

The Year 1 ROI multiple table (21x for Option A, 36x for Options B and C) at "low estimate" is the killer math slide. Even at 50% of every assumption, the recommended option still pays back inside 30 days and returns more than 10x in year one. Naming the margin in the model ("substantial margin built in") is what makes the math defensible against skeptical legal partners.

The Phase 1B credit clause ("if Phase 2 is signed within 30 days of Phase 1 completion, $5,000 of the Phase 1B fee credits toward the Phase 2 engagement") is the operational move that converts a sale into a two-phase contract without forcing Phase 2 commitment upfront. The credit creates a soft deadline without pressure.

The "lanes" section (Hüify delivers vs Petroff Amshen provides) is the operational rigor that prevents scope creep. Each side has a numbered list. Optional add-ons section creates upside without bloating the main scope.

The optional add-ons section creates upside without bloating the main scope: skeleton LP copy +$6K, skeleton drip email copy +$4.5K, conversion critique on existing drafts +$2.5K. The buyer can scope-up at signature.

# Petroff Amshen LLP - Site Map and Page Inventory

## What it is
Technical content inventory of petroffamshen.com (Webflow CMS) dated 2026-05-01, prepared as part of Phase 1A scope for the active Petroff Amshen engagement. Total estimated pages ~160: 6 top-level + 10 practice areas + 4 attorney bios + ~25 publications verified + ~110 marketing landing pages (per Marianne) + 1 verified NLP form + 1 standalone campaign + 3 legal/footer. Flags URL inconsistencies (Foreclosure Defense lives at both /practice-areas/foreclosure-attorneys and /practice-areas/foreclosure-defense), proposes a consolidated target structure for HubSpot migration, and lists 6 information items needed from the firm before Phase 2.

## Strategic thesis
**Audit first, migrate second, consolidate ruthlessly.** ~110 landing pages is sprawl. The team has already stated intent to "do a cleanse" and "reduce it a lot." The site map's purpose is not to migrate everything, it is to give the firm a defensible kill list. The keep-rule is explicit: 50+ monthly organic visits OR destination for an active paid campaign. Everything else 301-redirects to the nearest cousin.

The deeper move: split Phase 1 (4 priority practice area LPs live in Content Hub, running parallel to Webflow) from Phase 2 (full migration). Phase 1 captures attribution from ad traffic without breaking the existing site. Phase 2 happens after ROI evidence is in.

## What is interesting about this doc
The amber-box-vs-green-box format is the reusable structure. Amber = "FOR TEAM DISCUSSION" (open questions, decision items). Green = "HÜIFY RECOMMENDATION" (the prescriptive answer). Every section pairs the two. This format lets the firm see the gaps before they hear the answer, which builds trust faster than leading with the recommendation.

The 110-to-40-or-50 consolidation math is the operational rigor. Group structure: 4 priority practice areas × 8-12 variants each (geo, audience, intent) + 4-6 generic conversion pages. The math lands at 40-50. Naming the math prevents the team from arguing about whether the target should be 60 or 90 without a frame.

The three URL pattern resolution (/practice-areas/, /landing-pages/, /nlp-form/ + root campaigns) is the kind of clean-up problem most firms never address. The recommendation table proposes /lp/ as the new marketing folder, which is cleaner for analytics and easier to remember in conversation.

The "information to gather" section converts an audit into a procurement checklist: Webflow CMS export, Search Console top 1000 URLs, GA4 top landing pages, form schema, brand assets, existing 301 redirects. Each item is a concrete handoff request, not a vague ask.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any website audit, content inventory, or migration scoping:

body:
# Petroff Amshen Strategic Scoping (Managing Partners)

## What it is
Pre-meeting prep document dated 2026-04-23 for Serge F. Petroff (Managing Partner) ahead of the Wednesday April 29 2026 1:00 PM ET working session. Paired with [[petroff-amshen-operational-scoping-team]] (sent to the HubSpot/marketing ops lead). Walks through context Josh believes is true about the firm (HubSpot Pro stack in place, RocketMatter migration explicit goal, immediate work is Creative Hub + Marketing Hub buildout, Bogota marketing/intake teams, NJ expansion planned, ~50 retainers from NJ expected, foreclosure defense flat fee $50K+, FCRA contingency, broader consumer protection + appellate). Names Josh's bias (rebuild website as measurable intake engine not visual rebuild), explains what to expect on Wednesday minute-by-minute, lays out three likely paths after the meeting plus an explicit fourth "keep going internal, call us when something breaks" option, then poses 5 strategic questions for Serge to answer before they meet.

## Strategic thesis
**Match the document's depth to the buyer's sophistication.** "Pretending this is a simple buildout by lobbing a short vendor style intake form would waste your time." Serge is a former fintech founder with a $300M mortgage put option product. The doc explicitly names that recognition. Two paired documents (strategic for Serge, operational for the HubSpot/marketing ops lead) split sophistication levels so each gets the right shape of question.

The deeper move: **transparency about my bias as a pressure-test ask.** Josh explicitly names his bias ("rebuild website as measurable intake engine, not visual rebuild") and frames the strategic questions as the place where the buyer can pressure-test that bias. "If marketing is not the biggest lever for the firm in the next 12 months, I would rather tell you that than sell you a project in the wrong spot." This is the inverse of the standard sales doc which tries to hide the seller's predisposition. Naming the bias up-front makes the seller credible.

Third move: **four-paths menu including the no-sale option.** Three likely paths after April 29 (scoped Phase 1 buildout / paid migration audit / park and revisit) plus an explicit fourth ("keep going with internal build, call us when something breaks"). Naming the no-sale option is the credibility move that converts the meeting from a pitch to a consultation.

## What is interesting about this doc
The opening line addressed to Serge is itself a strategic move. "Thanks for the call and for starting the fresh email thread after. That was a clean handoff and it gave me what I needed to start shaping the right engagement before Wednesday." Naming a small competent thing the buyer did (starting a fresh email thread) signals attention to detail. Most sales follow-ups start with "Hope you had a great weekend."

The "How I think about this work" section is the IP statement. "When a law firm migrates its website and marketing function into HubSpot, the mistake most implementation partners make is treating it as a visual rebuild. Copy the current site, put it in HubSpot, ship it, invoice. That project is not hard and it is not valuable. Any partner with a HubSpot CMS team can do it. The project that actually moves the firm is rebuilding the website as a measurable intake engine. Same user experience on the surface. Underneath, every form submission, every call, every organic click is mapped to a lead source, a practice area, an intake owner, and a retainer outcome." This is the [[2026-case-os-framework]] thesis applied specifically to the website-and-marketing scope.

The Wednesday agenda minute-by-minute structure (0-10 team walks punch list / 10-30 Josh walks back his approach / 30-45 honest conversation about fit and sequencing / 45-60 agreement on next step) is unusually disciplined. Each segment has a named purpose. "I am not walking in with a prebaked proposal. The point on Wednesday is to get aligned, not to pitch. Any scoping or pricing conversation happens after I have earned the right to have it, which means after I understand your answers."

The "Three likely paths" section ends with "There is a fourth path, which is 'keep going with internal build, call us when something breaks.' That is a fine answer too, and I will tell you Wednesday if I think that is the right call." This converts the seller from advocate to advisor.

The five strategic questions:
1. Firm vision 12 months out (what does winning look like in real numbers)
2. Where retainers come from today (channel mix splits, rough is fine)
3. The biggest constraint on growth (people / marketing volume / case management throughput / geo / tech / capital / partner bandwidth / something else)
4. Competing priorities and capital (other 12-month investments and stack-rank by impact)
5. Decision process (partner consensus / ROI threshold / payback period / gut call / who else weighs in)

Each question has a "Why I am asking" one-liner. Question 3 explicitly says "If marketing volume is not the top constraint, I do not want to sell you more marketing." Question 4 explicitly invites the opportunity-cost conversation most vendors avoid.

"If a question does not have a confident answer, write that. 'We have not decided yet' or 'I do not know' is useful. Do not polish before returning. Unpolished is more useful than polished." This is the most underrated instruction in the corpus.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any high-ACV, sophisticated-buyer pre-meeting prep doc:

1. **Two-document partner-vs-team split** (strategic doc for managing partner, operational doc for ops lead, both pre-meeting). Drop into any high-stakes deal with sophisticated decision-makers and operational teams.
2. **"Transparency about my bias" section** (name your predisposition, frame the questions as pressure-test). Drop into any pre-meeting doc to convert seller from advocate to advisor.
3. **Four-paths menu with explicit no-sale option** (paths 1-3 are sales paths, path 4 is "keep doing what you're doing, call us when something breaks"). Drop into any pre-meeting doc where buyer skepticism is high.
4. **Minute-by-minute meeting agenda** (0-10 / 10-30 / 30-45 / 45-60 with named purpose per segment). Drop into any high-stakes working session.
5. **"I am not walking in with a prebaked proposal" disclaimer**. Drop into any pre-meeting doc where buyer fears being pitched.
6. **Five strategic questions** (12-month vision in real numbers / channel mix / biggest constraint / competing priorities / decision process). Drop into any high-ACV discovery.
7. **"Why I am asking" one-liners per question**. Drop into any survey or discovery instrument to anchor answers.
8. **"Unpolished is more useful than polished" instruction**. Drop into any pre-meeting doc to reduce buyer effort and increase answer quality.
9. **"How to complete this document" box at the top** with explicit steps and time budget (about 10 min). Drop into any pre-meeting prep doc.
10. **"How to return this document" green box at the close** with deadline, address, two methods. Drop into any returnable instrument.
11. **Opening line that names something specific the buyer did well** (started a fresh email thread). Drop into any high-touch sales follow-up.
12. **References mentioned by name + practice area + size** (Napoli Shkolnik mass tort NY+PR 250+, Hansen & Rosasco NYC 9/11, separate 9/11 firm) without belaboring. Drop into any legal vertical pitch.

## ROI / outcome / story
**Context Josh captured before sending:**
- HubSpot stack in place: Marketing Hub Pro, Content Hub Pro, Operations Hub Pro, Sales Hub Enterprise, seats configured
- Case management migration off RocketMatter is explicit goal (7 years on platform, evaluated Litify rejected for Salesforce-based, evaluated Cleo, HubSpot chosen)
- Immediate work: Creative Hub + Marketing Hub buildout, transition website and landing pages into HubSpot
- Marketing/intake teams in Bogota; partners in Brooklyn
- NJ expansion planned, ~50 retainers expected from NJ, more capacity on the way
- Pre-pandemic: one of largest foreclosure defense firms in state
- Practice mix today: foreclosure defense (flat fee from $50K), FCRA (contingency + fees), broader consumer protection, appellate

**Three likely paths after April 29:**
1. Scoped Phase 1 buildout: fixed fee scope, 3-6 weeks, website + landing page rebuild wired to HubSpot intake and CRM
2. Paid migration audit: 2 weeks focused audit, crawl + URL map + SEO risk + HubSpot architecture proposal + fixed fee rebuild proposal. Audit cost credits toward rebuild if proceed within 30 days.
3. Park and revisit: capital and attention invested elsewhere; Josh tells what he would do whether or not Huify involved
4. (Implicit) Keep going internal, call us when something breaks. "That is a fine answer too."

**Five questions (Serge's homework, due EOD Monday April 27):**
1. Firm vision 12 months out (2-3 real numbers that tell you it worked)
2. Channel mix splits across website/organic, paid ads, referrals, direct calls, other
3. Single biggest constraint on growth (pick one or add)
4. Other investments weighed in next 12 months + stack-rank
5. Decision process (partner consensus, ROI threshold, payback, gut, who weighs in)

- **Proposal downstream**: [[petroff-amshen-path-to-functional]] / [[petroff-amshen-marketing-content-operations]] / [[petroff-amshen-site-map]] (the proposals produced after the working session)

Patrick Maniego (HubSpot Partner channel) mentioned the firm on Feb 18 call before formal intro. **This doc** (2026-04-23): pre-meeting prep doc for Serge. Companion ops doc sent same day. **Next**: Serge returns answers by EOD Monday 2026-04-27. **Working session**: Wednesday 2026-04-29 1:00 PM ET, 60 minutes. **Downstream**: working session ([[petroff-amshen-working-session-4-29]]) produces site map ([[petroff-amshen-site-map]]) + proposal narrative ([[petroff-amshen-path-to-functional]]) + formal quote ([[petroff-amshen-marketing-content-operations]]) all dated 2026-05-01. **Long arc**: Phase 1 -> Phase 2 (Webflow migration separate engagement) -> Phase 3 (deeper ops + NJ expansion deferred).

body:
# Pioneer Metal Finishing - RFQ to Close Audit

## What it is
10-slide engagement overview pitch for Pioneer Metal Finishings dated 2026-04-28, prepared for David Jilot, Paul Lund, Chris Haasch. Frames a $30K, 30-day audit of Pioneer's RFQ-to-Close motion with a day-14 out clause ($15K max risk cap). Three deliverables: documented process map of every stage, hit-rate analysis on top 4 product categories, Phase 2 roadmap with hard ROI projections. Calibrated to a 2026-04-28 alignment, engagement letter signed by Friday May 1, kickoff Monday May 4, delivery week of June 1.

## Strategic thesis
**Brand gravity without a harvest motion is the most expensive gap a manufacturer can have.** Pioneer is "one of the more highly visited" players in metal finishing (David's words). The question is not how to get more traffic; it is how much of what they already have is being harvested. 30,000 quotes per year at 15% hit rate = 4,500 wins. One point of lift = +300 wins = +$8.7M incremental revenue at $29K average win value = +$3.5M EBITDA at 40% margin. The audit's job is to find where the existing flow leaks.

The deeper strategic move: **day-14 out clause caps Pioneer's exposure at $15K**. Audit is $30K total, but the buyer can terminate in writing at the day-14 midpoint review for any reason. This is a risk-reversed pitch that converts the buyer's decision from "will this $30K audit produce results" into "will the first 14 days produce enough signal to continue." Smaller decision = faster decision.

Third move: **6-stage walk** (RFQ Intake / Outlook Routing / Pricing Review / Sales Gophering / Quote Out / Win-Loss Loop) presented as a working hypothesis with the explicit ask "Walk it with us. Tell us where this matches and where it doesn't." Replaces the consultant-tells-you-your-process pattern with co-authorship.

## What is interesting about this doc
The priority tagging on Section 01 ("What We've Heard") is the rhetorical move. Each captured insight gets a tag: HIGH PRIORITY, VALIDATE, STRENGTH. Three buckets force the team to immediately see what is asserted vs what needs to be tested vs what is already working. Most discovery summaries flatten everything; this one shapes it.

"Outlook's gotta end" as a verbatim Paul Lund quote pinned at the top of HIGH PRIORITY is the kind of customer-voice anchor that proves the seller is listening. The audit will validate, quantify, or refute each hypothesis. Naming "validate or refute" leaves room for the audit to discover that a stated pain is not actually the biggest one.

The "What This Could Be Costing You" section reframes future risk as current cost: "These are not hypothetical future risks. They are current costs running every month the gaps stay open." Past Investment At Risk flag explicitly names that prior automation attempt did not yield (David flagged). This is candor that builds trust faster than glossing over a previous failure.

The math at One Point Lift ($8.7M revenue, $3.5M EBITDA) is calibrated for the manufacturer's brain. EBITDA at 40% margin is named, not assumed. The "Payback: less than one win" line at the bottom of the math slide is the closer.

The Pod section (Josh, Ben, Sergio, Erika) with named roles is the credibility move. Ben as CTO + Dynamics 365 + Azure architecture lead is unusually specific for a sales deck. Sergio's "Former HubSpot support team" framing is the legitimacy anchor. Most sales decks have generic team slides; this one names exactly who does what.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any manufacturing audit, RFQ-driven business, or risk-reversed engagement:

1. **Priority-tagged "What We've Heard" section** (HIGH PRIORITY / VALIDATE / STRENGTH tags). Drop into any discovery summary to shape attention.
2. **Day-14 out clause with $15K max risk cap**. Drop into any audit engagement where buyer risk is the gating concern.
3. **Six-stage process walk** (RFQ Intake / Routing / Pricing Review / Sales Gophering / Quote Out / Win-Loss). Drop into any manufacturing RFQ-to-close audit.
4. **One-point-lift math frame** (current state -> +1 point -> incremental revenue -> incremental EBITDA at margin). Drop into any pitch where you can quantify a small move against a large base.
5. **"What This Could Be Costing You" reframe** (current cost not hypothetical future risk). Drop into any pitch that needs to convert future uncertainty into present-tense pain.
6. **Past Investment At Risk flag** (acknowledge prior failed attempt explicitly). Drop into any pitch to a buyer who has been burned by a previous vendor.
7. **Walk-it-with-us co-authorship ask** (present the 6-stage hypothesis, ask the buyer to validate or correct it). Drop into any discovery framing.
8. **Audit deliverables formula** (Process Map + Hit Rate Analysis + Phase 2 Roadmap with hard ROI). Drop into any operational audit.
9. **Four-person Pod team slide** with named role per person. Drop into any sales deck where team credibility matters.
10. **Specific Tuesday-to-Friday-to-Monday timeline** (alignment Tue, letter Fri, kickoff Mon next week). Drop into any pitch with sign-today urgency.

## ROI / outcome / story
**Pioneer's current state:**
- $130M revenue
- 40% EBITDA
- 30,000 quotes per year
- 15% hit rate = 4,500 wins
- ~$29K average win value
- 3,700 pricing team hours per year (estimated)
- 11 divisions, 11 workflows (no standardization)

**One Point Lift (the math anchor):**
- 16% hit rate = 4,800 wins (+300 wins)
- +$8.7M incremental revenue (300 × $29K)
- +$3.5M EBITDA at 40% margin
- Payback: less than one win

**The Six-Stage RFQ-to-Close path:**
1. RFQ Intake (rfq@pioneermetal.com auto-acks in 60 sec; Josh's 3/26 RFQ as real example)
2. Outlook Routing (filtered by facility, manual triage in shared inbox)
3. Pricing Review (~3,700 hours/yr pricing team time)
4. Sales Gophering (sales calls customers for missing info; David: "information organizers")
5. Quote Out (30,000 quotes/yr at 15% hit rate = 4,500 wins)
6. Win/Loss Loop (currently undefined; audit makes this measurable)

**Audit engagement terms:**
- $30K total, 30 days, day-14 out clause, $15K max exposure
- Three deliverables: Process Map, Hit Rate Analysis, Phase 2 Roadmap
- Timeline: alignment Apr 28, letter Fri May 1, kickoff Mon May 4, midpoint review May 18, delivery week of June 1

## How this relates
- **GTM v2 deal**: named in [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] open pipeline ($30K Audit for CPQ Engine, Presentation Scheduled, 30%)
- **TortScale plan deal**: named in [[tortscale-readinessaudit-gtm-operating-plan-v2]] as tertiary ICP (Manufacturing) and Phase 1 close push
- **Vertical anchor**: Pioneer is the manufacturing parallel to H&R (legal) and Mediafly (SaaS) for the three-vertical funnel in [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]]
- **Stack note**: Pioneer runs Dynamics 365 + Azure + Power BI + ZoomInfo. NOT HubSpot. Ben's CTO role and Dynamics 365 architecture lead is the specific competency this deal needs.
- **Audit pattern sibling**: same audit-to-Phase-2 motion as the legal vertical audit ([[hansen-rosasco-ai-proof-extraction-plan]] was the design partner that produced this audit pattern)
- **Sibling Pioneer doc**: [[pioneer-engagement-letter]] (the formal terms)
- **Earlier prep**: [[pioneer-paul-1on1-prep]] (1:1 with Paul Lund)

## Evolution
**Earlier**: David Jilot, Paul Lund, Chris Haasch initial conversation. RFQ stack inventory (Dynamics 365, Azure, Power BI, ZoomInfo) confirmed. Prior automation attempt flagged as not yielding. **This doc** (2026-04-28): engagement overview pitch. **Next**: alignment session 2026-04-28, engagement letter by Friday 2026-05-01, kickoff Monday 2026-05-04. **Phase 1**: weeks of May 4 and May 11 discovery + interviews + data review. **Phase 1 midpoint**: 2026-05-18 day-14 review + out-clause window. **Phase 1 delivery**: week of June 1. **Phase 2**: decision and SOW (if approved) following week.

## When to consult this in the future
- Pitching an audit-to-Phase-2 engagement to a manufacturer
- Designing a day-14 out clause to cap buyer risk
- Building a 6-stage RFQ-to-Close process walk for any quote-driven business
- Framing brand-gravity-without-harvest for a high-traffic underconverting business

# SEDA Law Firm - Client Overview

## What it is
Oklahoma estate planning and probate firm. Active client since December 2025. Folder contains 3 files at top level: Lead Data Jan 12 2026 (60KB estate planning lead dataset), Online Accounts (basic), Pipeline Stages (10KB workbook). Engaged on the Option C "HubSpot Activation Lean Start" path defined in [[seda-law-decision-summary]] ($10-12K implementation, 2-4 weeks setup, deliberate Phase 0 to reduce risk before bigger investment).

## Strategic thesis
**Lean-start Phase 0 to earn the right to Phase B/C later.** SEDA chose Option C explicitly because of Q1 flat-fee rollout pressure and the March 2026 Lawcus renewal deadline. The deal is anchored to the renewal as a forcing function. "Option C earns Option B through usage and results."

The deeper move: SEDA is Huify's smallest active legal-vertical engagement, but proves the productized lean-start motion that becomes the Quick-Start Sprint at $5K in [[tortscale-readinessaudit-gtm-operating-plan-v2]]. SEDA is essentially the pilot client for the Sprint shape, even though the deal closed as a $12K "Intake HubSpot 1 Month" engagement.

## What is interesting about this client
The Pipeline Stages workbook (Jan 2026) and Lead Data spreadsheet (Jan 2026) indicate Huify started by stamping out the basic HubSpot infrastructure — pipeline stages and lead data hygiene — before automation. The intentional sparseness of the folder reflects the lean-start scope.

The architecture decision in [[seda-law-decision-summary]] is the interesting part: HubSpot for CRM/intake/automation, CosmoLex for billing+trust accounting (the hard part for any legal firm), PandaDoc for retainer packets, QuickBooks for GL. Keep-what-works applied to legal billing.

## Reusable assets / methodologies that emerged here
1. **Option C Lean Start playbook** — under $12K, 2-4 weeks, no automation yet, prove the foundation
2. **Four-tool legal architecture** — HubSpot + PandaDoc + CosmoLex + QuickBooks
3. **Lawcus sunset migration pattern** — small-firm legacy CRM exit
4. **Deal anchored to software renewal** — Lawcus March 2026 renewal as forcing function

## ROI / outcome / story
**Closed deal value (per [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] 2025 appendix):**
- SEDA Law, Intake HubSpot 1 Month: $12,462

**Projected ROI (per [[seda-law-decision-summary]] using Shelby's numbers):**
- 25 new engagements/month × $3,213 avg net = baseline
- Revenue lift: $144K-$286K/year
- Labor efficiency: ~$34K/year
- Marketing efficiency: ~$12K/year
- Total upside: $190K-$286K/year
- Year 2+ yearly net: ~$168K
- ROI Year 2+: ~141%

## How this relates
- **Deal-level deliverable**: [[seda-law-decision-summary]] is the decision document that produced this engagement
- **Era position**: [[huify-history-era-8-legal-documents-ai-2025-present]]

body:
# SEDA Law - Decision Summary & Executive Recommendation

## What it is
Two-part decision document for SEDA Law (Oklahoma estate planning / probate firm targeting $5M+ revenue and multi-office expansion). Part 1 (Decision Summary, December 2025) walks through three onboarding paths (A: Full Migration too-heavy / B: HubSpot Intake Engine full build / C: HubSpot Activation Lean Start, the new recommended entry point) with negotiated HubSpot pricing from Patrick. Part 2 (Executive Summary, earlier) lays out the four-tool architecture (HubSpot + PandaDoc + CosmoLex + QuickBooks) with ROI snapshot using Shelby's own numbers. Outcome: 2025 closed-won at $12,462 (Intake HubSpot 1 Month per [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] pipeline appendix).

## Strategic thesis
**Option C earns Option B through usage and results, not by forcing it upfront.** SEDA was in a price-and-change-management squeeze: Lawcus renewal in March, Q1 flat-fee rollout in progress, doesn't want to switch billing + CRM simultaneously, current stage ~$1M revenue. Option B (full intake engine $18.5K-$22.5K) was the right long-term architecture but more than necessary as a starting point. Option C (HubSpot Activation, $10K-$12K with 10% upfront discount) is the deliberate Phase 0 that reduces risk, preserves cash, and lets results justify deeper investment later. "All work carries forward into Option B later."

The deeper strategic move: **deal anchored to a real external event (March Lawcus renewal)**. SEDA had explicit dates to beat. The proposal sequences "December-March: Implementation Phase 1" against the renewal cliff. No anchor = no urgency. Naming the renewal date converts SEDA's procrastination into a forcing function.

Third move: **four-tool architecture that respects existing complexity**. HubSpot for CRM/intake/automation/marketing/attribution. PandaDoc for retainer packets and multi-doc signatures. CosmoLex for billing + hourly/flat-fee invoicing + trust accounting (3-way reconciliation, IOLA-compliant). QuickBooks for firm-level accounting. WhatConverts short-term for attribution data feeding HubSpot. This is the keep-what-works frame ([[carpenter-john-recommended-path]]) applied to the legal-billing stack.

## What is interesting about this doc
The A/B/C options structure with explicit "Option C does NOT replace Option B; it earns Option B through usage" is the rhetorical move that converts the rescope from "we cheaped out" to "we sequenced this right." The buyer can see the same final architecture either way; the choice is just the entry point.

The HubSpot pricing section directly quoting Patrick's negotiated numbers (Option 1 budget path $13,392/year discounted from $19,380 = ~$6K discount; Option 2 Professional Customer Platform $14,400/year discounted from $23,400 = $9K discount) is unusually transparent. Most agencies hide HubSpot pricing inside a bundled implementation fee. This doc separates Huify implementation from HubSpot software explicitly, which builds trust faster.

The ROI Snapshot uses Shelby's own numbers (25 new engagements/month, $3,213 avg net per engagement, 3 intake staff = ~$11,300/month, ~$7,980/mo marketing, ~$10K/year current software). The math derives:
- Revenue lift: $144K-$286K/year
- Labor efficiency: ~$34K/year
- Marketing efficiency: ~$12K/year
- Total upside: $190K-$286K/year
- Year 1 net profit after costs: ~$120K expected
- Year 2+ yearly net: ~$168K
- ROI Year 2+: ~141%

Using the buyer's own numbers rather than industry benchmarks is the difference between "math you might believe" and "math you cannot dispute."

The billing-and-trust-architecture section (Intake -> Retainer -> Matter Creation -> Billing & Trust) names the exact handoff workflow: HubSpot manages forms/routing/scheduling/comms, PandaDoc generates retainer packet, signed retainer triggers HubSpot to "Retainer Signed," HubSpot triggers automatic Matter creation inside CosmoLex, Matter ID syncs back to HubSpot for reporting, CosmoLex handles trust balance + ledger + 3-way recon + invoicing, QuickBooks remains GL. This is the operational architecture diagram in prose. It is the level of detail that closes a legal-firm deal.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any legal-firm CRM proposal, multi-tool architecture decision, or phase-0-lean-start motion:

1. **Three onboarding options A/B/C** (full migration / full build / lean start with "Option C earns Option B through results"). Drop into any proposal where the right long-term architecture exceeds the buyer's current appetite.
2. **Four-tool architecture for legal firms** (HubSpot + PandaDoc + CosmoLex + QuickBooks + optional WhatConverts). Drop into any law-firm-billing proposal.
3. **Billing-and-trust architecture workflow** (Intake -> Retainer -> Matter Creation -> Billing & Trust, with each system named per step). Drop into any legal-billing handoff design.
4. **Negotiated HubSpot pricing quoted from Patrick directly** with line items + discount math. Drop into any HubSpot Solutions Partner cosell.
5. **ROI Snapshot using buyer's own numbers** (5 inputs from Shelby -> 4 named upside categories -> Year 1 net + Year 2+ net + ROI%). Drop into any proposal where buyer-provided numbers are available.
6. **Deal anchored to external event** (Lawcus March renewal as forcing function). Drop into any deal that needs a real date to act against.
7. **Verdict box per option** (high value but too heavy / right architecture but more than necessary / smartest starting point right now). Drop into any A/B/C decision document.
8. **"How to Think About These Options" summary table** (Do everything now / Build the full intake engine / Get live, get confident, then expand). Drop into any phased options framing.
9. **10% upfront discount option** (for Option C if paid in full vs structured payments). Drop into any pricing for a cash-tight buyer.
10. **"December-March Implementation Phase 1" sequencing against renewal cliff**. Drop into any deal where timing pressure exists.

## ROI / outcome / story
**Closed outcome (per [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] 2025 closed-won appendix):**
- "Seda Law, Intake HubSpot 1 Month" = $12,462

**Decision options at time of doc:**
- Option A (Full Migration): $45K-$52K implementation, $30K-$33K/year software, 12-16 weeks. Verdict: too heavy for Q1.
- Option B (Full Intake Engine + keep Lawcus short-term): $18,500 upfront or $22,500 over 3 months, ~$1,750/mo software, 60-75 days. Verdict: right long-term architecture, may be more than needed now.
- Option C (HubSpot Activation Lean Start, recommended): $10K-$12K implementation, same HubSpot subscription, 2-4 weeks. Verdict: smartest starting point.

**The ROI math (using Shelby's numbers):**
- 25 new engagements/month × $3,213 avg net per engagement
- Revenue lift: $144K-$286K/year
- Labor efficiency: ~$34K/year
- Marketing efficiency: ~$12K/year
- Total upside: $190K-$286K/year
- Year 1 net profit: ~$120K
- Year 2+ yearly net: ~$168K
- ROI Year 2+: ~141%

**The four-tool stack (annual software cost):**
- HubSpot Pro: ~$14.4K/year
- CosmoLex: ~$8.5K/year
- PandaDoc: ~$3.6K/year
- Zapier/Integration: ~$1.2K/year
- WhatConverts: ~$1.2K-$2.4K/year
- GoToConnect: unchanged
- QuickBooks: unchanged
- Total new stack: ~$33K/year vs old stack ~$10K/year = ~$23K/year delta (fully offset by ROI lift)

## How this relates
- **Sibling lean-start pattern**: Option C is the same shape as [[tortscale-readinessaudit-gtm-operating-plan-v2]]'s $5K Quick-Start Sprint and [[mediafly-sizzle-deck]]'s $3K Launch SKU. All three converge on the under-CFO-discretionary-spend entry point with auto-renew or natural Phase 2.
- **Keep-what-works architecture**: [[carpenter-john-recommended-path]]'s "HubSpot engagement layer + MyCase case management + Page medical AI" is the same architecture pattern as SEDA's "HubSpot CRM + CosmoLex billing/trust + QuickBooks GL + PandaDoc retainers"
- **Partner channel**: Patrick Maniego (HubSpot) is the partner who negotiated SEDA's pricing. Same Patrick referenced in [[petroff-amshen-marketing-content-operations]] (Feb 18 call before formal intro). Patrick is a recurring partner node.
- **GTM v2 closed-won record**: $12,462 listed in [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] 2025 closed-won appendix

All three are professional services / consumer protection sub-vertical candidates per [[huify-horizontal-expansion-gtm]]

## Evolution

Compared Lawmatics, Lawcus, HubSpot, CosmoLex, Zoho, Salesforce, hybrid options. **This doc** (2025-12-08, modified 2026-03-11): final decision document. **Closed**: 2025, "Intake HubSpot 1 Month" at $12,462. **Long arc**: if Option C results justify, expand to Option B (full intake engine) and eventually Option A (full migration including billing/trust to CosmoLex).

body:
# TortScale & ReadinessAudit.com GTM Operating Plan v2

## What it is
The parent 90-day GTM operating plan dated 2026-05-04 covering window 2026-05-04 to 2026-08-02. Defines the two-engine model: Engine 1 (Huify Services, cash engine, ReadinessAudit.com front door, Quick-Start Sprint as recurring product) and Engine 2 (Documents AI by TortScale Inc, the product bet, equity vehicle). Locks two SKUs only: $5K Quick-Start Sprint (2 weeks, auto-renews at $5K floor / $7.5K standard / $10K+ heavy every 4 weeks) and $15K AI Readiness Audit (6 weeks, evaluation-mode buyers only, credits 100% to first 90 days of Sprints). Hard kill checkpoint: May 31, 2026.

## Strategic thesis
**Two engines, one funds the other, AI compresses the discovery layer that traditional consulting bills humans for.** Engine 1 (Huify Services) generates cash and creates reference customers for Engine 2 (Documents AI by TortScale). Engine 2 is what TortScale Inc eventually raises against and sells as a product. The strategic axis that makes the $5K / 2-week promise credible is "AI as the analysis engine" — Claude agents do discovery in days that humans previously did in weeks, humans drive execution. That is the differentiator, the margin story, and the speed-to-value promise in one sentence.

The deeper move: hard kill checkpoint at May 31. If 0 paying Sprint clients by then, audit dies, Ben pauses Documents work, all-in HubSpot services until cash stabilizes. The pre-committed kill criterion forces the team to either prove the Sprint funnel or stop pretending it works. Most operating plans never name a kill threshold; this one does.

The third strategic move: replace the three-step model (Diagnostic + Implementation Fee + Retainer) with one continuous AI-driven value-priced engagement that auto-renews. The buyer never sees a contract negotiation until they want to cancel. The auto-renewal mechanic is what converts a buyer trial into recurring revenue without a separate upsell event.

## What is interesting about this doc
The "retired offers" section is unusually disciplined. Six prior SKUs explicitly killed: $2.5K Readiness Audit + $500 first-10 promo (replaced by Sprint), $25K-$40K AI Due Diligence (replaced by $15K Audit), $40K-$50K Assessment + Roadmap (bundled into Sprint), Intake Optimization Sprint (now an initiative inside a Sprint), Attribution Roadmap (same), $15K one-time HubSpot implementation fee (absorbed), long-form retainers (replaced by 4-week auto-renewal). Naming what is dead is what makes the new SKU stack credible.

The lane-A vs lane-B sales motion split is the operational rigor. Lane A (cold/DM/Loom -> self-checkout) is the high-volume low-friction motion where AEs never touch a contract. Lane B (HubSpot rep co-sell -> structured discovery) is the higher-ACV motion where the rep flags launch-mode vs evaluation-mode at first call and routes accordingly. Both lanes converge on Sprint cycles within 8 weeks.

The two-question routing rule at the start of every co-sell discovery call is the cleanest sales decision aid in the document:
1. Is this a launch-mode buyer (-> Sprint) or evaluation-mode buyer (-> Audit)?
2. What is the first initiative if launch-mode?

The financial reality section is unusually candid: $110K cash, $21K/mo contracted MRR, $29K/mo break-even, $8K/mo burn, 13 months runway. "One paying Sprint at Heavy tier ($10K/4 wks) closes a third of the gap. Three Sprints at Standard tier closes it entirely." That arithmetic discipline converts the GTM into a survival math problem with clear thresholds.

The decision log section separates "LOCKED on May 4" (9 decisions) from "still OPEN, bring to Friday alignment" (10 decisions). Every plan should do this. Most do not.

## Reusable assets
Lift these for any productized-services GTM, two-engine model, or value-priced auto-renewal motion:

1. **Two-engine model** (cash engine funds product bet, product bet's reference customers come from cash engine). Drop into any services-to-product transition.
2. **AI as the engine** value-prop axis (Claude/agents compress discovery, humans drive execution). Drop into any productized-services value-prop where you need to justify a 14-day promise against an 8-week traditional norm.
3. **Quick-Start Sprint + auto-renew tier ladder** ($5K entry / 2 weeks, then $5K-$7.5K-$10K+ tiers every 4 weeks, cancel-anytime with 14 days notice). Drop into any recurring services motion.
4. **AI Readiness Audit as trust-transfer product** ($15K for evaluation-mode buyers only, 100% credit to first 90 days of Sprints if they engage). Drop into any motion where some buyers need to be convinced before committing operationally.
5. **Lane A (self-checkout) vs Lane B (co-sell discovery) parallel sales motion**. Drop into any GTM that wants both low-friction and high-ACV paths.
6. **Two-question routing rule** at first call (launch-mode vs evaluation-mode + first initiative). Drop into any discovery call structure.
7. **Hard kill checkpoint with explicit criteria** (May 31, 0 paying Sprints = audit dies, Ben pauses Documents, all-in services). Drop into any operating plan to force a pre-committed pivot vs sunk cost.
8. **Retired offers section** (explicit list of dead SKUs to prevent re-introduction). Drop into any pricing reset.
9. **Default-to-Sprint-over-Audit rule** (unless buyer is verifiably in evaluation mode). Drop into any motion where you have a wedge and a fuller offer and need a rule for which to lead with.
10. **Auto-renewal mechanic without contract event** (buyer sees day-21 renewal pre-notice, can cancel by day 14 of next cycle). Drop into any subscription motion to convert trials into recurring revenue silently.
11. **Tier-upgrade rescope discipline** (default to same tier as prior cycle; tier upgrades require explicit rescope conversation, not silent inflation). Drop into any tiered subscription.
12. **RACI per stage table** (12 stages from hand-raiser content to Documents pilot rollout). Drop into any multi-stage service delivery operation.
13. **Hire only on binding constraint rule** (5 named roles, each with explicit trigger). Drop into any hiring plan to prevent premature hires.
14. **Risk-mitigation table** (likelihood / impact / mitigation per risk, 9 risks named). Drop into any operating plan.
15. **Decision log split** (LOCKED vs OPEN, with OPEN items routed to next alignment). Drop into any working operating doc.
16. **Disqualification triggers** (4 explicit, e.g., below $5M revenue, no marketing/ops leader, deep on Salesforce/Litify, "build us an AI chatbot" as buying signal). Drop into any ICP filter.

## ROI / outcome / story
**The math at time of plan:**
- Cash on hand: ~$110K
- Contracted MRR: $21K/mo across 2 clients
- Break-even: $29K/mo
- Monthly burn: ~$8K
- Runway: ~13 months
- One paying Sprint at Heavy tier ($10K/4 wks) closes 1/3 of the gap
- Three Sprints at Standard tier closes the gap entirely

**The proof anchor (H&R):**
- $526K closed across two deals (Sales Enterprise/ENT Bundle $446K + Intake Bundle $79.8K)
- 14,000 active claims
- 600K documents under management
- 700GB live in production today
- Productized into Documents AI by TortScale (HIPAA-compliant DMS native to HubSpot)
- HubSpot deprecated their native Documents feature in 2025, opening the marketplace gap
- Legal DMS market forecast: $5.9B by 2033

**90-day Sprint targets:**
- Phase 1 (May 4 - May 31): 1+ paying (kill threshold) / 3+ target / AI discovery automation operational / readinessaudit.com v2 live
- Phase 2 (Jun 1 - Jun 28): 5+ paying / 70%+ renewal rate / 1+ tier upgrade / 2nd Documents partner committed
- Phase 3 (Jun 29 - Aug 2): 10+ paying / 70%+ ongoing renewal / 3 Documents design partners / marketplace listing technically ready / TortScale Inc raise materials drafted

**Channel weekly cadence:**
- LinkedIn (Josh): 5 posts/week
- Loom outbound: 25 Looms/week
- HubSpot Partner intros: 2 active/week minimum
- Podcast: 1/month

## How this relates
- **Sibling 90-day plan**: [[huify-gtm-writeup-v2]] is the content-led tactical operating layer; this is the strategic parent. They were authored 4 days apart and reference each other implicitly
- **Engine 1 proof**: leans on [[hansen-rosasco-year-one-review-deck]] / [[hansen-rosasco-ai-proof-extraction-plan]] as the design-partner story
- **Engine 2 product**: Documents AI by TortScale Inc is the productized version of the [[huify-documents-platform]] built for H&R
- **Active Phase 1 deals**: [[carpenter-john-recommended-path]] + [[carpenter-chartered-discovery-2026-05-05]] + [[carpenter-chartered-cosell-playbook]] (Carpenter as Phase 1 close push), Hall Benefits Law (in flight, reframe to Sprint), Mediafly ([[mediafly-sizzle-deck]] - separate Plus One motion), Petroff Amshen (warm via Patrick)
- **Expansion brief sibling**: [[huify-horizontal-expansion-gtm]] uses H&R as wedge proof; this plan defines the engine that produces more proof points
- **Operational truth**: [[huify-skills-scheduled-tasks-analysis]] is the operational footprint of how Huify executes (8 scheduled skills, 5 consolidated, 4×/day on the top skills)
- **Content engine dependency**: explicitly out of scope here, lives in josh-identity / Second Brain workstream
- **Documents GTM**: explicitly separate doc, owner Josh, due before end of May
- **Parent entity decisions**: TortScale Inc Delaware C-Corp filing target May 15, IP assignment from Huify LLC to TortScale Inc, BillLowerGuys side-project-only

## Evolution
**Earlier**: April 27 v1 of this plan. Three-step model (Diagnostic + Implementation + Retainer) plus multiple specialized sprints (Intake Optimization, Attribution Roadmap). Long-form retainers. **This doc** (2026-05-04): v2 supersedes v1, consolidates to two SKUs, locks AI-as-engine value-prop axis, names hard kill checkpoint. **Phase 1**: weeks 1-4 (May 4 - May 31) ship the Sprint, hit kill threshold or pivot. **Phase 2**: weeks 5-8 (Jun 1 - Jun 28) scale Sprints + 2nd Documents partner. **Phase 3**: weeks 9-13 (Jun 29 - Aug 2) productionize + raise prep. **Long arc**: if Phase 3 hits, TortScale Inc raises against Documents product; if Sprint funnel underperforms at kill checkpoint, all-in services until cash stabilizes.

## When to consult this in the future
- Designing any productized-services GTM with a two-engine cash-and-product split
- Pricing a recurring auto-renewal product against a one-time audit alternative
- Writing a hard kill checkpoint into an operating plan
- Compressing traditional consulting discovery via AI-augmented analysis
- Structuring lane A self-checkout vs lane B co-sell discovery as parallel motions
- Building a tier ladder ($5K / $7.5K / $10K+) that prevents silent inflation
- Designing RACI for a multi-stage service delivery operation
- Drafting a hire-only-on-binding-constraint hiring plan
- Naming retired offers explicitly to prevent re-introduction
- Splitting decision log into LOCKED vs OPEN items

## Open decisions (still on the Friday alignment list)
1. Documents pricing model (per-seat / per-document-volume / flat tier)
2. NewCo equity allocation (Josh / Ben / advisor split)
3. Sergio role under two-engine model
4. TortScale Inc entity status + IP assignment from Huify LLC
5. TortScale Notion teamspace naming
6. HubSpot Payments vs Stripe for Sprint checkout
7. Carpenter Chartered scope (Sprint + Audit, or Documents design partner from day one)
8. Hall Benefits Law commercial close (reframe to Sprint motion)
9. Brand naming for Documents (Documents AI by TortScale vs ClientDocs vs new mark)
10. AI discovery automation scope (which agent flows ship by week 1 vs week 4)
